    simpa only [Function.update_apply, neg_inj, he] using h
  · funext i
    rfl
  · exact List.append_nil _

/-- The finite transduction lemma for the return sweep, with the exact cost. -/
lemma sweep_run_reverse {A S R C : Type} (tm : MultiTapeTM 1 A S)
    (state : R → S) (symbol : C → A) (visit : R → C → R × C)
    (htr : ∀ s a inp, tm.tr (state s) inp (fun _ => some (symbol a)) =
      sweepAct (state (visit s a).1) (some (symbol (visit s a).2)) .neg)
    {x : List A} (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (out : List A)
    (as : List C) (s : R) (z : ℤ) (l r : List (Option A)) :
    tm.runFrom (sweepRevCfg (some (state s)) p z l
      (as.map (fun a => some (symbol a)) ++ r) out) as.length =
    sweepRevCfg (some (state (sweepFold visit s as).1)) p (z - as.length)
      (((sweepFold visit s as).2.map (fun a => some (symbol a))).reverse ++ l) r out := by
  induction as generalizing s z l with
  | nil => simp only [List.map_nil, List.nil_append, List.length_nil,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, sweepFold, Int.natCast_zero, sub_zero, List.reverse_nil]
  | cons a as ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.cons_append, List.length_cons]
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
    have hr : (sweepRevCfg (some (state s)) p z l
        (some (symbol a) :: (as.map (fun a => some (symbol a)) ++ r)) out).workTapeSymbols =
        fun _ => some (symbol a) := by
      funext i
      exact sweepTape_read (-z) l _
    change tm.runFrom ((tm.tr (state s) _ _).apply _) as.length = _
    rw [hr, htr, sweepRevCfg_left, ih]
    simp only [sweepFold, List.map_cons, List.reverse_cons, List.append_assoc,
      List.cons_append, List.nil_append, Int.natCast_add, Int.natCast_one]
    congr 1
    omega

/-- Turning round exchanges the two finite stacks. -/
lemma sweepTape_turn {A : Type} (z : ℤ) (l r : List (Option A)) :
    sweepTape z l r = fun w => sweepTape (-(z - 1)) r l (-w) := by
  funext w
  by_cases h : w < z
  · have h' : ¬ -w < -(z - 1) := by omega
    have he : -w - -(z - 1) = z - 1 - w := by omega
    simp only [sweepTape, if_pos h, if_neg h', he]
  · have h' : -w < -(z - 1) := by omega
    have he : -(z - 1) - 1 - -w = w - z := by omega
    simp only [sweepTape, if_neg h, if_pos h', he]

/-- Concatenating two scans threads the finite control between them. -/
lemma sweepFold_append {R C : Type} (visit : R → C → R × C)
    (s : R) (as bs : List C) :
    sweepFold visit s (as ++ bs) =
      let first := sweepFold visit s as
      let second := sweepFold visit first.1 bs
      (second.1, first.2 ++ second.2) := by
  induction as generalizing s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a as ih => simp only [List.cons_append, sweepFold, ih]

/-- A transducer whose state is a table, changing only the entry named by a cell. -/
def indexedVisit {I V C : Type} [DecidableEq I]
    (visit : I → V → C → V × C) (s : I → V) (a : I × C) :
    (I → V) × (I × C) :=
  let v := visit a.1 (s a.1) a.2
  (Function.update s a.1 v.1, (a.1, v.2))

/-- On a block with distinct tape indices, each local rule sees the original
table entry. This is the block invariant for both sweeps.
**Proof sketch.** Induct on the index list. The first update does not affect
any remaining index because the list has no duplicates. For the final table,
split an arbitrary queried index into the first index, a tail member, or neither. -/
lemma indexedFold {I V C : Type} [DecidableEq I]
    (visit : I → V → C → V × C) (cell : I → C) (is : List I) (hi : is.Nodup)
    (s : I → V) :
    sweepFold (indexedVisit visit) s (is.map (fun i => (i, cell i))) =
      (fun i => if i ∈ is then (visit i (s i) (cell i)).1 else s i,
        is.map (fun i => (i, (visit i (s i) (cell i)).2))) := by
  induction is generalizing s with
  | nil => simp [sweepFold]
  | cons i is ih =>
    obtain ⟨hin, ht⟩ := List.nodup_cons.mp hi
    simp only [List.map_cons, sweepFold, indexedVisit]
    rw [ih ht]
    apply Prod.ext
    · funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst j
        simp [hin]
      · simp only [Function.update_of_ne hj, List.mem_cons]
        by_cases hm : j ∈ is <;> simp [hj, hm]
    · dsimp only
      congr 1
      apply List.map_congr_left
      intro j hj
      have hji : j ≠ i := by rintro rfl; exact hin hj
      simp only [Function.update_of_ne hji]

/-- Each simulated tape contributes exactly one cell to an interleaved block. -/
lemma indexedFold_block {k : ℕ} {V C : Type}
    (visit : Fin k → V → C → V × C) (cell : Fin k → C) (s : Fin k → V) :
    sweepFold (indexedVisit visit) s ((List.finRange k).map (fun i => (i, cell i))) =
      (fun i => (visit i (s i) (cell i)).1,
        (List.finRange k).map (fun i => (i, (visit i (s i) (cell i)).2))) := by
  simpa only [List.mem_finRange, ↓reduceIte] using
    indexedFold visit cell (List.finRange k) (List.nodup_finRange k) s


/-- The return sweep's block rule is valid in reverse tape-index order too. -/
lemma indexedFold_block_reverse {k : ℕ} {V C : Type}
    (visit : Fin k → V → C → V × C) (cell : Fin k → C) (s : Fin k → V) :
    sweepFold (indexedVisit visit) s (((List.finRange k).map (fun i => (i, cell i))).reverse) =
      (fun i => (visit i (s i) (cell i)).1,
        ((List.finRange k).map (fun i => (i, (visit i (s i) (cell i)).2))).reverse) := by
  rw [← List.map_reverse, ← List.map_reverse]
  simpa only [List.mem_reverse, List.mem_finRange, ↓reduceIte] using
    indexedFold visit cell (List.finRange k).reverse
      (by simpa using List.nodup_finRange k) s


/-- One blank cell can be made explicit at the end of the zipper. -/
lemma sweepTape_nil {A : Type} (z : ℤ) (l : List (Option A)) :
    sweepTape z l [] = sweepTape z l [none] := by
  funext p
  unfold sweepTape
  split
  · rfl
  · cases (p - z).toNat <;> rfl

/-- The forward write identity also applies beyond the stored zone. -/
lemma sweepCfg_right_any {A S : Type} {x : List A} (q : Option S) (q' : S)
    (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (z : ℤ) (l r : List (Option A)) (out : List A)
    (b : Option A) :
    (sweepAct q' b .pos).apply (sweepCfg q p z l r out) =
      sweepCfg (some q') p (z + 1) (b :: l) r.tail out := by
  cases r with
  | cons a r => exact sweepCfg_right q q' p z l r out a b
  | nil =>
    have hc : sweepCfg q p z l ([] : List (Option A)) out =
        sweepCfg q p z l [none] out := by
      refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ rfl rfl
      funext i
      exact sweepTape_nil z l
    rw [hc]
    exact sweepCfg_right q q' p z l [] out none b

/-- The backward write identity also applies beyond the stored zone. -/
lemma sweepRevCfg_left_any {A S : Type} {x : List A} (q : Option S) (q' : S)
    (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (z : ℤ) (l r : List (Option A)) (out : List A)
    (b : Option A) :
    (sweepAct q' b .neg).apply (sweepRevCfg q p z l r out) =
      sweepRevCfg (some q') p (z - 1) (b :: l) r.tail out := by
  cases r with
  | cons a r => exact sweepRevCfg_left q q' p z l r out a b
  | nil =>
    have hc : sweepRevCfg q p z l ([] : List (Option A)) out =
        sweepRevCfg q p z l [none] out := by
      refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ rfl rfl
      funext i w
      exact congrFun (sweepTape_nil (-z) l) (-w)
    rw [hc]
    exact sweepRevCfg_left q q' p z l [] out none b

/-- A fixed finite sequence of writes, in either direction, takes its exact
length. The hypothesis is the local controller rule, and has no global-run premise. -/
lemma sweep_generate {A S : Type} {x : List A}
    (tm : MultiTapeTM 1 A S) (w : List A)
    (cfg : Fin (w.length + 1) → ℤ → List (Option A) → List (Option A) → Cfg 1 A S x)
    (d : ℤ)
    (hstep : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < w.length) z l r,
      tm.step (cfg ⟨i, by omega⟩ z l r) =
        cfg ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩ (z + d) (some w[i] :: l) r.tail)
    (z : ℤ) (l r : List (Option A)) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ w.length) :
    tm.runFrom (cfg 0 z l r) n =
      cfg ⟨n, by omega⟩ (z + d * n) ((w.take n).map some |>.reverse |>.append l)
        (r.drop n) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega), hstep n (by omega)]
    have hz : z + d * n + d = z + d * (n + 1 : ℕ) := by push_cast; ring
    rw [hz, List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]
    simp only [Option.toList_some, List.map_append, List.map_cons, List.map_nil,
      List.reverse_append, List.reverse_cons, List.reverse_nil, List.nil_append,
      List.cons_append, ← List.drop_one, List.drop_drop]
    rfl


/-- Source heads and nonblank cells stay within the elapsed-time interval.
**Proof sketch.** Heads start at zero and move by at most one per step.
A write can only change the cell under an old head, so it cannot create a
nonblank cell outside the larger interval at the next time. -/
lemma source_bounds {Γ : Type} (M : FinTM Γ) (x : List Γ) (t : ℕ) :
    (∀ i, -(t : ℤ) ≤ (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapePos i ∧
      (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapePos i ≤ t) ∧
    (∀ i z, z < -(t : ℤ) ∨ (t : ℤ) < z →
      (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapes i z = none) := by
  induction t with
  | zero => simp [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    constructor
    · intro i
      have hp := M.tm.workTapePos_step_le (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t) i
      rw [abs_le] at hp
      have := ih.1 i
      push_cast
      omega
    · intro i z hz
      have hz' : z < -(t : ℤ) ∨ (t : ℤ) < z := by omega
      have hne : z ≠ (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapePos i := by
        have := ih.1 i
        omega
      unfold MultiTapeTM.step
      cases hs : (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).state with
      | none => exact ih.2 i z hz'
      | some q =>
        dsimp only [Action.apply]
        cases hw : ((M.tm.tr q (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).inputSymbol
          (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).workTapeSymbols).workTapes i).1
        · exact ih.2 i z hz'
        · dsimp only
          rw [Function.update_of_ne hne]
          exact ih.2 i z hz'

end Turing.FinTM

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/UnaryTape.lean =====

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Logic.Function.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.SplitIfs

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Unary work tapes

A work tape (`ℤ → Option Bool`, as in `Turing.Cfg`) holding a natural number `m` in unary:
cells `0, …, m - 1` hold `1` and every other cell is blank. Machines that keep counters on
their work tapes in unary — the Tseitin emitter of
`TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.CircuitSatReductionMachineTapes` and the counter
programs of `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProg` — increment a counter by writing
`1` on its first blank cell and decrement it by erasing its last cell.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.UnaryTape.ones` — the unary tape of `m`.
* `Turing.UnaryTape.wrT` — the effect of an optional write at a head position.

## Main results

* `Turing.UnaryTape.update_ones_succ`, `Turing.UnaryTape.update_ones_pred` — increment and
  decrement.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the multi-tape machine.)
-/

namespace Turing

namespace UnaryTape

/-- The unary tape of a counter with value `m`: cells `0, …, m - 1` hold `1`. -/
def ones (m : ℕ) : ℤ → Option Bool := fun c => if 0 ≤ c ∧ c < m then some true else none

/-- A unary tape holds `1` on the cells `0, …, m - 1`. -/
theorem ones_lt {m : ℕ} {c : ℤ} (h0 : 0 ≤ c) (h : c < m) : ones m c = some true := by
  simp [ones, h0, h]

/-- A unary tape is blank from cell `m` on. -/
theorem ones_ge {m : ℕ} {c : ℤ} (h : (m : ℤ) ≤ c) : ones m c = none := by
  simp only [ones]; rw [if_neg]; omega

/-- A unary tape is blank left of cell `0`. -/
theorem ones_neg {m : ℕ} {c : ℤ} (h : c < 0) : ones m c = none := by
  simp only [ones]; rw [if_neg]; omega

/-- The unary tape of `0` is blank. -/
theorem ones_zero : ones 0 = fun _ => none := by
  funext c; simp only [ones]; rw [if_neg]; omega

/-- Writing `1` on the first blank cell of the unary tape of `m` gives that of `m + 1`. -/
theorem update_ones_succ (m : ℕ) :
    Function.update (ones m) (m : ℤ) (some true) = ones (m + 1) := by
  funext c
  simp only [Function.update_apply, ones]
  split_ifs <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)

/-- Erasing the last cell of the unary tape of `j + 1` gives that of `j`. -/
theorem update_ones_pred (j : ℕ) :
    Function.update (ones (j + 1)) (j : ℤ) none = ones j := by
  funext c
  simp only [Function.update_apply, ones]
  split_ifs <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)

/-- Writing at a head position: no write leaves the tape unchanged, a write `some s` sets
the cell `pos` to `s`. -/
def wrT (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (pos : ℤ) : Option (Option Bool) → ℤ → Option Bool
  | none => tape
  | some s => Function.update tape pos s

end UnaryTape

end Turing

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Asymptotic/Adversary.lean =====

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PPT
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machines as adversaries of the concrete experiments

The bridge between the machine layer (`Complexity.NUPPT`, strings `List Bool`) and the
concrete security experiments of `TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments` (typed
inputs `Fin m → Bool`, adversaries as functions of the input and of a uniform coin string).
An `NUPPT` `A` activated at parameter `n` becomes

* an *inverter* `A.inverter n ℓ m : (Fin m → Bool) → A.Coins n → Option (Fin ℓ → Bool)`
  [PS10, Definitions 27.3, 28.4]: `A(1^n, y)` with the output decoded as an `ℓ`-bit string;
* its literal variant `A.inverterLit ℓ m` for [PS10, Definition 26.1] (`A(f(x))`, activation
  at the input length `m`, no `1^n`);
* a *distinguisher* / *predictor* `A.distinguisher n m`, `A.predictor n m`
  [PS10, Definitions 69.4, 75.2, 78.3]: `A(1^n, t) = 1`, i.e. the output is the string `[true]`;
  `A.distinguisherL n` takes an untyped sample.

Inversion with a possibly failing decoder is `invProbOpt` (the probability that the decoded
output is a preimage); it is bridged to the concrete `invProb` by `invProbOpt_le_invProb`
(any default for a failure can only increase the probability) and `invProbOpt_some` (a total
inverter has the same probability). Foundation decision D5: inverses are sought in the
domain at the current parameter, and a wrong-length output counts as failure.

The file also records that "computes `f` with probability one" [PS10, Definition 24.6]
is, on the finite uniform coin space, the same as "for every coin string"
(`Complexity.NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob`), which justifies the frozen form of
`Complexity.NUPPT.Computes`.

**Deviation:** `inverter`: wrong-length output = failure (D5); verdict `= [true]` (normalisable
by `ifEq`).

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.coinBlock` — the common indexed coin-tape segment.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.decodeFin` — decode a string as an `ℓ`-bit string, failure on a wrong
  length; `TCSlib.Cryptography.padFin` — pad/truncate (for samplers).
* `Complexity.NUPPT.inverter`, `Complexity.NUPPT.inverterLit` — an `NUPPT` as an inverter
  (with `1^n`, and literal).
* `Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisher`, `Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisherL`,
  `Complexity.NUPPT.predictor` — an `NUPPT` as a distinguisher / predictor.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.invProbOpt` — inversion probability of a possibly failing inverter.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.coinBlock_eq`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.length_coinBlock` — the segment
  equation and its full-length condition.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.decodeFin_ofFn`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.padFin_ofFn` — decoding and
  padding invert `List.ofFn`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.invProbOpt_le_invProb`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.invProbOpt_some` — the
  bridges to the concrete `invProb`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.invProbOpt_nonneg`, `TCSlib.Cryptography.invProbOpt_le_one` — bounds.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob` — probability one is every coin string
  [PS10, Definition 24.6].

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.1–2.2: Definitions 24.6, 26.1, 27.3; §3.1–3.3: Definitions 69.4, 75.2, 78.3.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, Definitions 2.1, 2.3, 3.2–3.4 (the concrete experiments).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Complexity Turing Finset

/-- The `i`-th segment of `B` bits of a coin string; a short final segment is truncated. -/
def coinBlock (B i : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : List Bool := (r.drop (i * B)).take B

/-- The defining equation of `coinBlock`: `coinBlock B i r = (r.drop (i·B)).take B`. -/
theorem coinBlock_eq (B i : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : coinBlock B i r = (r.drop (i * B)).take B := rfl

/-- A coin segment has exactly `B` bits when its end lies within the input tape. -/
theorem length_coinBlock {B i : ℕ} {r : List Bool} (h : (i + 1) * B ≤ r.length) :
    (coinBlock B i r).length = B := by
  simp only [coinBlock_eq, List.length_take, List.length_drop]
  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at h
  omega

/-- Decode a string as an `ℓ`-bit string: `some` of its bits if the length is exactly `ℓ`,
`none` otherwise (a wrong-length answer of an inverter is a failure, D5). -/
def decodeFin (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Option (Fin ℓ → Bool) :=
  if h : w.length = ℓ then some (fun i => w.get (Fin.cast h.symm i)) else none

/-- The defining equation of `decodeFin`: `decodeFin ℓ w` is `some` of the bits of `w` when
`|w| = ℓ`, and `none` otherwise. -/
theorem decodeFin_eq (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    decodeFin ℓ w = if h : w.length = ℓ then some (fun i => w.get (Fin.cast h.symm i)) else none :=
  rfl

/-- Pad with `false` or truncate a string to exactly `ℓ` bits (the output convention of
samplers, where no failure is possible). -/
def padFin (ℓ : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Fin ℓ → Bool := fun i => w.getD i false

/-- Decoding the encoding of an `ℓ`-bit string returns it. -/
theorem decodeFin_ofFn {ℓ : ℕ} (x : Fin ℓ → Bool) : decodeFin ℓ (List.ofFn x) = some x := by
  simp [decodeFin]

/-- A decoded string has exactly the decoded length. -/
theorem length_eq_of_decodeFin_eq_some {ℓ : ℕ} {w : List Bool} {x : Fin ℓ → Bool}
    (h : decodeFin ℓ w = some x) : w.length = ℓ := by
  by_contra hw
  simp [decodeFin, hw] at h

/-- Padding the encoding of an `ℓ`-bit string returns it. -/
theorem padFin_ofFn {ℓ : ℕ} (x : Fin ℓ → Bool) : padFin ℓ (List.ofFn x) = x := by
  funext i
  simp [padFin]

/-- `A(1^n, y)` as an inverter: output decoded as an `ℓ`-bit string, wrong length = failure
[PS10, Definitions 27.3 and 28.4, the experiment `f(A(1^n, y)) = y`].

**Deviation:** wrong-length output = failure (D5). For a typed family this loses nothing. For
a string function `f : {0,1}* → {0,1}*` the text's experiment also accepts a preimage of
another length, so the typed experiment can count fewer successes and typed one-wayness is
implied by, but weaker than, the text's, unless `|f(x)|` determines `|x|` (length-regular `f`
whose output length is a non-constant `PolyExpr`, hence injective in the input length; with
constant output length neither notion is satisfiable). The proviso is stated where string functions enter the typed world,
`FunFamily.ofString` (`Asymptotic/OneWay.lean`; gate 03a, note 15). -/
def _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.inverter (A : NUPPT) (n ℓ m : ℕ) :
    (Fin m → Bool) → A.Coins n → Option (Fin ℓ → Bool) :=
  fun y r => decodeFin ℓ (A.runAt n (List.ofFn y) r)

/-- The literal inverter `A(y)` of [PS10, Definition 26.1]: activation at parameter `|y| = m`
(the text gives the adversary `f(x)` only; the `1^{|y|}` prefix carries no information). -/
def _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.inverterLit (A : NUPPT) (ℓ m : ℕ) :
    (Fin m → Bool) → A.Coins m → Option (Fin ℓ → Bool) :=
  fun y r => decodeFin ℓ (A.runAt m (List.ofFn y) r)

/-- `A(1^n, t)` as a distinguisher: accepts iff the output is the string `[true]`
[PS10, Definition 69.4]. -/
def _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisher (A : NUPPT) (n m : ℕ) :
    (Fin m → Bool) → A.Coins n → Bool :=
  fun t r => decide (A.runAt n (List.ofFn t) r = [true])

/-- `A(1^n, w)` as a distinguisher of untyped samples (ciphertexts, views, histories). -/
def _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisherL (A : NUPPT) (n : ℕ) : List Bool → A.Coins n → Bool :=
  fun w r => decide (A.runAt n w r = [true])

/-- The defining equation of `distinguisherL`:
`A.distinguisherL n w r = decide (A.runAt n w r = [true])`. -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisherL_eq (A : NUPPT) (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool)
    (r : A.Coins n) : A.distinguisherL n w r = decide (A.runAt n w r = [true]) := rfl

/-- `A(1^n, y)` as a predictor of a bit: the same verdict convention as a distinguisher
[PS10, Definitions 75.2 and 78.3]. -/
def _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.predictor (A : NUPPT) (n m : ℕ) :
    (Fin m → Bool) → A.Coins n → Bool :=
  A.distinguisher n m

/-- The literal inverter is the inverter at parameter `m`. -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.inverterLit_eq (A : NUPPT) (ℓ m : ℕ) :
    A.inverterLit ℓ m = A.inverter m ℓ m := rfl

/-- The typed distinguisher is the untyped one on `List.ofFn t`. -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.distinguisher_eq (A : NUPPT) (n m : ℕ) (t : Fin m → Bool)
    (r : A.Coins n) : A.distinguisher n m t r = A.distinguisherL n (List.ofFn t) r := rfl

/-- The predictor is the distinguisher. -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.predictor_eq (A : NUPPT) (n m : ℕ) :
    A.predictor n m = A.distinguisher n m := rfl

/-- The inverter succeeds on `(y, r)` iff the machine's output is the encoding of some `x'`. -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.inverter_eq_some_iff (A : NUPPT) (n ℓ m : ℕ) (y : Fin m → Bool)
    (r : A.Coins n) (x' : Fin ℓ → Bool) :
    A.inverter n ℓ m y r = some x' ↔ A.runAt n (List.ofFn y) r = List.ofFn x' := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hw : (A.runAt n (List.ofFn y) r).length = ℓ := length_eq_of_decodeFin_eq_some h
    simp only [NUPPT.inverter, decodeFin, dif_pos hw, Option.some.injEq] at h
    subst h
    refine List.ext_get (by simp [hw]) fun i h₁ h₂ => ?_
    simp
  · intro h
    show decodeFin ℓ _ = _
    rw [h, decodeFin_ofFn]

/-- The probability that a possibly failing inverter `A`, given `f x` for uniform `x` and
uniform coins, outputs `some x'` with `f x' = f x` (the typed experiment of
[PS10, Definition 27.3] with a wrong-length output counted as failure, D5). -/
noncomputable def invProbOpt {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] (f : α → β)
    (A : β → ρ → Option α) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun z : α × ρ => ∃ x', A (f z.1) z.2 = some x' ∧ f x' = f z.1

/-- The defining equation of `invProbOpt`:
`invProbOpt f A = Pr_{(x, r)}[∃ x', A(f x, r) = some x' ∧ f x' = f x]`, over uniform
`(x, r) ∈ α × ρ`. -/
theorem invProbOpt_def {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] (f : α → β)
    (A : β → ρ → Option α) :
    invProbOpt f A = uprob fun z : α × ρ => ∃ x', A (f z.1) z.2 = some x' ∧ f x' = f z.1 := rfl

/-- Replacing a failure by any default can only increase the inversion probability: the
bridge from `invProbOpt` to the concrete `invProb` [Gar26, Definition 2.1]. -/
theorem invProbOpt_le_invProb {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] [Inhabited α] (f : α → β)
    (A : β → ρ → Option α) :
    invProbOpt f A ≤ invProb f (fun y r => (A y r).getD default) := by
  refine uprob_mono ?_
  rintro ⟨x, r⟩ ⟨x', hx', hf⟩
  simp [hx', hf]

/-- A total inverter has the same probability under both conventions. -/
theorem invProbOpt_some {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] (f : α → β) (A : β → ρ → α) :
    invProbOpt f (fun y r => some (A y r)) = invProb f A := by
  unfold invProbOpt invProb
  congr 1
  funext z
  simp

/-- The inversion probability is nonnegative. -/
theorem invProbOpt_nonneg {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] (f : α → β)
    (A : β → ρ → Option α) : 0 ≤ invProbOpt f A :=
  uprob_nonneg _

/-- The inversion probability is at most one. -/
theorem invProbOpt_le_one {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] (f : α → β)
    (A : β → ρ → Option α) : invProbOpt f A ≤ 1 :=
  uprob_le_one _

/-- An event of probability one holds everywhere (private copy of
`TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit.forall_of_uprob_eq_one`, which lives in a frozen file). -/
private theorem forall_of_uprob_eq_one {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] {p : Ω → Prop}
    (h : uprob p = 1) (ω : Ω) : p ω := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter] at h
  have hc : (Fintype.card Ω : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0; rw [h0, div_zero] at h; exact zero_ne_one h
  have hcard : (univ.filter p).card = Fintype.card Ω := by
    have := (div_eq_one_iff_eq hc).1 h
    exact_mod_cast this
  have := Finset.eq_univ_of_card _ hcard
  have hω : ω ∈ univ.filter p := by rw [this]; exact mem_univ ω
  exact (mem_filter.1 hω).2

/-- **"With probability one" is "for every coin string"** [PS10, Definition 24.6]: `A`
computes `f` in the frozen sense (`Complexity.NUPPT.Computes`, equality for every coin
string) iff at every parameter and argument the event `A(1^n, y; r) = f(⟨1^n, y⟩)` has
probability one over the uniform coins. (On a finite uniform space an event of probability
one is the whole space.) -/
theorem _root_.Complexity.NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob (A : NUPPT) (f : List Bool → List Bool) :
    A.Computes f ↔
      ∀ n y, uprob (fun r : A.Coins n => A.runAt n y r = f (NUPPT.advInput n y)) = 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h n y
    have hp : (fun r : A.Coins n => A.runAt n y r = f (NUPPT.advInput n y)) = fun _ => True :=
      funext fun r => propext ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => h n y r⟩
    rw [hp, uprob_true]
  · intro h n y r
    exact forall_of_uprob_eq_one (h n y) r

end TCSlib.Cryptography

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Repetition
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Encryption

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The iterated block encryptor and tuple decryptor

The honest iterated machines behind the public-key constructions of [PS10, §3.10]: the
**block encryptor** `blockEncFun E L B` which, on the state word `⟨u, ⟨pk, ⟨m, r⟩⟩⟩`, encrypts the
consecutive `L(|u|)`-bit blocks of the message string `m` under the public key `pk` with a fresh
`B(|u|)`-coin segment of `r` each, returning the nested-pair tuple of the ciphertexts; and the
**tuple decryptor** `decListFun Dc` which, on `⟨sk, ⟨c₀, ⟨c₁, …⟩⟩⟩`, concatenates `Dc ⟨sk, cᵢ⟩`.
With one-bit blocks they are the encryptor and decryptor of the bitwise scheme built from a
single-bit secure scheme [PS10, p. 103]; with `n`-bit blocks the encryptor is the
"efficiently generate encryptions of any message, without knowing the secret key" step of the
hybrid reductions of the single ⇒ multi-message theorem for public-key encryption
[PS10, p. 103] and of the multi-value hiding of commitments [PS10, Theorem 126.4]. Both are
instances of `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit` (D11), with the unfolding lemmas
`blockEncFun_spec`, `blockList_ofFn`, `decListFun_spec` proved.

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.blockState`, `blockStep`, `blockEmit`, `blockEncFun`, `blockList` — the
  block encryptor, its step, emission and ideal output.
* The common `TCSlib.Cryptography.coinBlock` from `Asymptotic.Adversary` supplies coin segments.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.decListStep`, `decListEmit`, `decListFun` — the tuple decryptor.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.blockEncFun_spec`, `blockList_ofFn` — unfolding of the block encryptor.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.blockEncFun_poly`, `decListFun_poly` — both machines are polynomial-time.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.decListFun_spec` — unfolding of the tuple decryptor.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.encodeList_eq_flatMap`, `pairEncode_nil_append`,
  `length_le_length_encodeList` — the tuple encoding as a concatenation of blocks.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§3.10, p. 103; §4.6, Theorem 126.4.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Complexity Turing
open PrivateKeyScheme (encodeList)

/-! ## The tuple encoding as a concatenation of blocks -/

/-- The nested-pair encoding is the concatenation of the self-delimiting blocks `⟨c, []⟩`. -/
theorem encodeList_eq_flatMap (l : List (List Bool)) :
    encodeList l = l.flatMap fun c => pairEncode c [] := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons c cs ih => simp [encodeList, ih, pairEncode]

/-- A tuple encoding is at least as long as the tuple. -/
theorem length_le_length_encodeList (l : List (List Bool)) :
    l.length ≤ (encodeList l).length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons c cs ih => simp only [encodeList, length_pairEncode, List.length_cons]; omega

/-! ## The iterated block encryptor and decryptor -/

/-- The state word `⟨u, ⟨pk, ⟨m, r⟩⟩⟩` of the block encryptor: unary parameter `u`, public key
`pk`, remaining message `m`, remaining coins `r`. -/
def blockState (u pk m r : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode u (pairEncode pk (pairEncode m r))

/-- A block state is the nested pair encoding of its parameter, key, message and coins. -/
theorem blockState_eq (u pk m r : List Bool) :
    blockState u pk m r = pairEncode u (pairEncode pk (pairEncode m r)) := rfl

/-- One step of the block encryptor: drop `L(|u|)` message bits and `B(|u|)` coins. -/
def blockStep (L B : PolyExpr) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  blockState (pairFstD w) (pairFstD (pairSndD w))
    ((pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))).drop (L.eval (pairFstD w).length))
    ((pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))).drop (B.eval (pairFstD w).length))

/-- The emission of the block encryptor: nothing once the message is exhausted, otherwise the
block `⟨E ⟨⟨⟨u, ⟨pk, m.take L⟩⟩, []⟩, r.take B⟩, []⟩` (the evaluator `E` is an `NUPPT.output` run
on the uniform layout with the next coin segment). The emptiness test is written in the shape
of `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe`. -/
def blockEmit (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : PolyExpr) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if decide ((pairSndD (pairEncode [] (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))))).length ≤
      (pairFstD (pairEncode [] (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))))).length) then []
  else pairEncode (E (NUPPT.layout (pairFstD w)
    (pairEncode (pairFstD (pairSndD w))
      ((pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))).take (L.eval (pairFstD w).length)))
    [] ((pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD w))).take (B.eval (pairFstD w).length)))) []

/-- The **block encryptor**: on a state word `x = ⟨u, ⟨pk, ⟨m, r⟩⟩⟩`, the concatenation of the
emissions along `|x| + 1` steps — the nested-pair tuple of the encryptions of the consecutive
`L(|u|)`-bit blocks of `m` under `pk`, each with a fresh `B(|u|)`-coin segment of `r`. -/
def blockEncFun (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (x.length + 1)).flatMap fun i => blockEmit E L B ((blockStep L B)^[i] x)

/-- The block encryptor concatenates the emissions of rounds `0, …, |x|` from `x`. -/
theorem blockEncFun_eq (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) :
    blockEncFun E L B x =
      (List.range (x.length + 1)).flatMap fun i => blockEmit E L B ((blockStep L B)^[i] x) := rfl

/-- The ideal list of block encryptions with fuel `k`: `[]` once the message is empty. -/
def blockList (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : ℕ) (u pk : List Bool) :
    ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List (List Bool)
  | 0, _, _ => []
  | k + 1, m, r => if m = [] then [] else
      E (NUPPT.layout u (pairEncode pk (m.take L)) [] (r.take B)) ::
        blockList E L B u pk k (m.drop L) (r.drop B)

/-- Unfolding: the step on a state word. -/
theorem blockStep_blockState (L B : PolyExpr) (u pk m r : List Bool) :
    blockStep L B (blockState u pk m r) =
      blockState u pk (m.drop (L.eval u.length)) (r.drop (B.eval u.length)) := by
  simp [blockStep, blockState]

/-- Unfolding: the emission on a state word. -/
theorem blockEmit_blockState (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : PolyExpr) (u pk m r : List Bool) :
    blockEmit E L B (blockState u pk m r) = if m = [] then [] else
      pairEncode (E (NUPPT.layout u (pairEncode pk (m.take (L.eval u.length))) []
        (r.take (B.eval u.length)))) [] := by
  simp [blockEmit, blockState, List.length_eq_zero_iff]

/-- The projections of the empty word are empty. -/
private theorem pairFstD_nil : pairFstD [] = [] := rfl

/-- The projections of the empty word are empty. -/
private theorem pairSndD_nil : pairSndD [] = [] := rfl

/-- The block `⟨c, []⟩` followed by a tuple is the tuple extended by `c`. -/
theorem pairEncode_nil_append (c w : List Bool) :
    pairEncode c [] ++ w = pairEncode c w := by
  simp [pairEncode]

/-- **Unfolding of the block encryptor** on a state word: with `k` rounds and a message of at
most `k · L(|u|)` bits (`L(|u|) > 0`), the concatenated emissions are the nested-pair tuple of
`blockList` with fuel `k + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `k` generalizing `m, r`: `List.range_succ_eq_map` splits off the
first emission (`blockEmit_blockState`); the remaining emissions are those of the state after
one step (`Function.iterate_succ_apply`, `blockStep_blockState`), covered by the induction
hypothesis at `m.drop L` (`List.length_drop`), and `pairEncode_nil_append` reassembles the
tuple; an empty message emits nothing forever. -/
theorem blockEncFun_spec (E : List Bool → List Bool) (L B : PolyExpr) (u pk : List Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (m r : List Bool), m.length ≤ k * L.eval u.length →
      ((List.range (k + 1)).flatMap fun i =>
        blockEmit E L B ((blockStep L B)^[i] (blockState u pk m r))) =
      encodeList (blockList E (L.eval u.length) (B.eval u.length) u pk (k + 1) m r) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro m r hm
    have hm0 : m = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp (by simpa using hm)
    subst hm0
    simp [blockEmit_blockState, blockList, encodeList]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro m r hm
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [Function.iterate_zero, id, Function.iterate_succ_apply, blockStep_blockState]
    by_cases hm0 : m = []
    · subst hm0
      simp only [List.drop_nil]
      rw [ih [] (r.drop (B.eval u.length)) (by simp)]
      simp [blockEmit_blockState, blockList, encodeList]
    · rw [ih (m.drop (L.eval u.length)) (r.drop (B.eval u.length)) (by
        rw [List.length_drop, Nat.add_mul, one_mul] at *
        omega)]
      simp only [blockEmit_blockState, hm0, if_false, blockList, encodeList]
      exact pairEncode_nil_append _ _

/-- A step grows a word by at most six symbols (an invalid word collapses to the empty state).

**Proof sketch.** Case analysis on the validity of the three nested pairs (`pairDecode`
`none` versus `eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode`); `length_pairEncode`, `List.length_drop`. -/
private theorem length_blockStep_le (L B : PolyExpr) (w : List Bool) :
    (blockStep L B w).length ≤ w.length + 6 := by
  have key : ∀ z : List Bool, (pairFstD z = [] ∧ pairSndD z = []) ∨
      2 * (pairFstD z).length + 2 + (pairSndD z).length = z.length := by
    intro z
    cases hz : pairDecode z with
    | none => exact Or.inl ⟨by simp [pairFstD, hz], by simp [pairSndD, hz]⟩
    | some p =>
      obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := p
      rw [eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z a b hz]
      exact Or.inr (by simp [length_pairEncode])
  simp only [blockStep, blockState, length_pairEncode, List.length_drop]
  rcases key w with ⟨hw1, hw2⟩ | hw
  · simp only [hw1, hw2, pairFstD_nil, pairSndD_nil, List.length_nil]
    omega
  rcases key (pairSndD w) with ⟨ht1, ht2⟩ | ht
  · simp only [ht1, ht2, pairFstD_nil, pairSndD_nil, List.length_nil]
    omega
  rcases key (pairSndD (pairSndD w)) with ⟨hs1, hs2⟩ | hs
  · simp only [hs1, hs2, List.length_nil]
    omega
  omega

/-- Orbit bound for a step that grows words by at most `c` symbols. -/
private theorem length_iterate_le {g : List Bool → List Bool} {c : ℕ}
    (hg : ∀ w, (g w).length ≤ w.length + c) (x : List Bool) :
    ∀ i, (g^[i] x).length ≤ x.length + c * i := by
  intro i
  induction i with
  | zero => simp
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    have := hg (g^[i] x)
    rw [Nat.mul_succ]
    omega

/-- The block step is polynomial-time (pair projections, `polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly`). -/
theorem blockStep_poly (L B : PolyExpr) : PolyTimeComputable (blockStep L B) := by
  have hu := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hpk := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hm := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hr := polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have h := hu.pairEncode (hpk.pairEncode
    (((polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly L).comp (hu.pairEncode hm)).pairEncode
      ((polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly B).comp (hu.pairEncode hr))))
  convert h using 1
  funext w
  simp [blockStep, blockState, Function.comp]

/-- The block emission is polynomial-time for a polynomial-time `E`
(`polyTimeComputable_ite`, `polyTimeComputable_lenLe`, `polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly`,
`NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_layout`). -/
theorem blockEmit_poly {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) (L B : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable (blockEmit E L B) := by
  have hu := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hpk := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hm := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hr := polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hp := polyTimeComputable_lenLe.comp ((polyTimeComputable_const []).pairEncode hm)
  have hbody := (hE.comp (NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_layout hu
    (hpk.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly L).comp (hu.pairEncode hm)))
    (polyTimeComputable_const []) ((polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly B).comp (hu.pairEncode hr)))).pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_const [])
  have h := polyTimeComputable_ite hp (polyTimeComputable_const []) hbody
  convert h using 1
  funext w
  simp only [blockEmit, Function.comp, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]

/-- **The block encryptor is polynomial-time**: an instance of
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit` with `R := var` rounds and the orbit bound
`7 · |x|` (`length_blockStep_le`, `length_iterate_le`). -/
theorem blockEncFun_poly {E : List Bool → List Bool} (hE : PolyTimeComputable E) (L B : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable (blockEncFun E L B) := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit (blockStep_poly L B) (blockEmit_poly hE L B)
    .var (.mul (.const 7) .var) (fun x i hi => by
      have := length_iterate_le (length_blockStep_le L B) x i
      simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var] at hi
      simp only [PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
      nlinarith)
  exact h

/-- One step of the tuple decryptor on `⟨sk, cs⟩`: drop the first ciphertext. -/
def decListStep (w : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (pairFstD w) (pairSndD (pairSndD w))

/-- The emission of the tuple decryptor on `⟨sk, cs⟩`: nothing once the tuple is exhausted,
otherwise `Dc ⟨sk, c₀⟩` (test in the shape of `polyTimeComputable_lenLe`). -/
def decListEmit (Dc : List Bool → List Bool) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if decide ((pairSndD (pairEncode [] (pairSndD w))).length ≤
      (pairFstD (pairEncode [] (pairSndD w))).length) then []
  else Dc (pairEncode (pairFstD w) (pairFstD (pairSndD w)))

/-- The **tuple decryptor**: on `x = ⟨sk, ⟨c₀, ⟨c₁, …⟩⟩⟩` the concatenation
`Dc ⟨sk, c₀⟩ ++ Dc ⟨sk, c₁⟩ ++ ⋯` along `|x| + 1` steps. -/
def decListFun (Dc : List Bool → List Bool) (x : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (List.range (x.length + 1)).flatMap fun i => decListEmit Dc (decListStep^[i] x)

/-- The defining equation of `decListFun`: the emissions of rounds `0, …, |x|`, concatenated. -/
theorem decListFun_eq (Dc : List Bool → List Bool) (x : List Bool) :
    decListFun Dc x =
      (List.range (x.length + 1)).flatMap fun i => decListEmit Dc (decListStep^[i] x) := rfl

/-- **Unfolding of the tuple decryptor**: with `k ≥ |l|` rounds on `⟨sk, encodeList l⟩` the
emissions concatenate to `l.flatMap (fun c => Dc ⟨sk, c⟩)`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `k` generalizing `l`, cases on `l`; `List.range_succ_eq_map`,
`Function.iterate_succ_apply`; the step on `⟨sk, ⟨c, rest⟩⟩` is `⟨sk, rest⟩` and the step on
`⟨sk, []⟩` is `⟨sk, []⟩`. -/
theorem decListFun_spec (Dc : List Bool → List Bool) (sk : List Bool) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (l : List (List Bool)), l.length ≤ k →
      ((List.range (k + 1)).flatMap fun i => decListEmit Dc (decListStep^[i] (pairEncode sk (encodeList l)))) =
        l.flatMap fun c => Dc (pairEncode sk c) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro l hl
    have hl0 : l = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp (by simpa using hl)
    subst hl0
    simp [decListEmit, encodeList]
  | succ k ih =>
    intro l hl
    rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [Function.iterate_zero, id, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    cases l with
    | nil =>
      have hstep : decListStep (pairEncode sk (encodeList [])) = pairEncode sk (encodeList []) := by
        simp [decListStep, encodeList, pairSndD_nil]
      rw [hstep, ih [] (by simp)]
      simp [decListEmit, encodeList]
    | cons c cs =>
      have hstep : decListStep (pairEncode sk (encodeList (c :: cs))) = pairEncode sk (encodeList cs) := by
        simp [decListStep, encodeList]
      rw [hstep, ih cs (by simpa using hl)]
      simp [decListEmit, encodeList, length_pairEncode]

/-- The tuple decryptor's step grows a word by at most two symbols. -/
private theorem length_decListStep_le (w : List Bool) : (decListStep w).length ≤ w.length + 2 := by
  simp only [decListStep, length_pairEncode]
  cases hz : pairDecode w with
  | none =>
    simp [pairFstD, pairSndD, hz, pairDecode]
  | some p =>
    obtain ⟨a, b⟩ := p
    rw [eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode w a b hz]
    simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, length_pairEncode]
    have : (pairSndD b).length ≤ b.length := by
      cases hb : pairDecode b with
      | none => simp [pairSndD, hb]
      | some p' =>
        obtain ⟨a', b'⟩ := p'
        rw [eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode b a' b' hb]
        simp [length_pairEncode]
    omega

/-- **The tuple decryptor is polynomial-time** for a polynomial-time `Dc`
(`polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit`, `R := var`, orbit bound `7 · |x|`). -/
theorem decListFun_poly {Dc : List Bool → List Bool} (hD : PolyTimeComputable Dc) :
    PolyTimeComputable (decListFun Dc) := by
  have hstep : PolyTimeComputable decListStep :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hemit : PolyTimeComputable (decListEmit Dc) := by
    have hp := polyTimeComputable_lenLe.comp
      ((polyTimeComputable_const []).pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
    have h := polyTimeComputable_ite hp (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      (hD.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
        (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)))
    convert h using 1
  have h := polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit hstep hemit .var (.mul (.const 7) .var)
    (fun x i hi => by
      have := length_iterate_le length_decListStep_le x i
      simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var] at hi
      simp only [PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_var]
      nlinarith)
  exact h

/-- `blockList` with one-bit blocks and enough fuel on an `n`-bit message is the list of the `n`
bit encryptions with the consecutive coin segments.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n`; `List.ofFn_succ` splits off the first bit, the fuel is a
successor, and the segments of `r.drop B` are the shifted segments of `r` (`List.drop_drop`). -/
theorem blockList_ofFn (E : List Bool → List Bool) (B : ℕ) (u pk : List Bool) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Bool) (r : List Bool) (k : ℕ), n ≤ k →
      blockList E 1 B u pk k (List.ofFn m) r =
        List.ofFn fun i : Fin n => E (NUPPT.layout u (pairEncode pk [m i]) [] (coinBlock B i r)) := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro m r k _
    cases k <;> simp [blockList]
  | succ n ih =>
    intro m r k hk
    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k', k = k' + 1 := ⟨k - 1, by omega⟩
    rw [List.ofFn_succ, List.ofFn_succ]
    simp only [blockList, List.cons_ne_nil, if_false, List.take_succ_cons, List.take_zero,
      List.drop_succ_cons, List.drop_zero, coinBlock_eq, Fin.val_zero, zero_mul, List.cons.injEq,
      true_and]
    rw [ih (fun i => m i.succ) (r.drop B) k (by omega)]
    congr 1
    funext i
    simp only [coinBlock_eq, Fin.val_succ, List.drop_drop]
    rw [show (B + ↑i * B) = (↑i + 1) * B by ring]

end TCSlib.Cryptography
