import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.Defs
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.InteractiveProofs

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Sequential composition of zero-knowledge proofs (statement phase)

[PS10, Theorem 175.1]: if `(P, V)` is a perfect or computational zero-knowledge proof for `L`
and `Q` is a polynomial, the protocol `(P_Q, V_Q)` that runs `(P, V)` on the common input `x`
`Q(|x|)` times in sequence, each time with fresh coins, is again a perfect or computational
zero-knowledge interactive proof.

**The construction** (`Protocol.seqRep`), on the interaction model of
`ZeroKnowledge/Interaction.lean` (D8): with `k = rounds(|x|)` moves of `π`, phase `j` occupies
the `2k` moves `2kj, …, 2kj + 2k − 1`.
- The first `k` moves of a phase are `π`'s; in the last `k` (**fillers**) the honest parties
  send `[]`. A phase thus has an even number of moves, so every phase starts with the same mover
  as `π` (`moverIsV_two_mul_add`), even when `k` is odd (the graph protocols have three
  messages). Each party moves exactly `k` times per phase.
- A party finds the global move from the number of messages it has received
  (`proverMoveIndex_exec`, `verifierMoveIndex_exec`), hence its phase `j` and position `t`.
  At a position `t < k` it runs `π`'s next-message function on the coin slice `j` of its tape
  (`coinBlock` from `Asymptotic/Adversary.lean`) and on the messages received in phase `j`
  (all of them real, since `t < k`).
- The coins of `P_Q` and `V_Q` are `Q` copies of `π`'s.
- `V_Q`'s verdict, on its complete history (`Q · k` messages), is `[true]` iff every phase's
  verdict, `V.next` on that phase's real messages, is `[true]`; otherwise `[false]`. When
  `π.verifierFirst = false`, `V_Q` makes the last move, and by the convention of D8 that move is
  its verdict (`outV_eq_getLast_of_moverIsV`); the filler position carries it, and nobody
  reads it.

**Deviations** (beyond D8, declared once here).
- **Filler moves**, as above: each phase is padded to `2k` moves; the honest parties' fillers
  are `[]` and are ignored.
- **Strict-PPT simulators and bounded abort retries** (ruling G02-#4, D8): zero-knowledge
  composes to zero-knowledge, and statistical error `δ` composes to `Q · δ`. The formal
  `PerfectZKAbort` premise is [Gol01, Definition 4.3.1]'s strict-PPT aborting formulation:
  abort probability at most `1/2`, and the exact real-view law conditioned on success.
  `PerfectZKAbort.statZK` runs this simulator on `n = |x|` independent fresh coin blocks,
  keeping the first non-aborting output. All retries abort with probability at most `2^{-n}`,
  giving statistical error `2^{-n}`; composition gives `Q(n) · 2^{-n}`. Each retry is already
  strict PPT. [PS10]'s expected-polynomial-time wording is a separate source convention;
  this bounded-retry argument does not assert that arbitrary expected-time truncation
  preserves an exact conditional output law.
- **Bounded prover messages** (`Protocol.ProverBounded`). Under D8, `Strategy.Efficient` bounds
  a verifier's work per activation in the total length of its input, not in `|x|`. A cheating
  `V_Q` may then double its message length in every phase. If the honest prover echoes the
  verifier's messages, which is zero-knowledge for one run, the views of `V_Q` grow like
  `2^{Q(|x|)}`, which no strict PPT simulator can output. The composition theorems therefore
  assume that the honest prover's messages on instances with witnesses have at most `B(|x|)`
  bits. The text's machines read only `t(|x|)` bits per message, so the issue does not arise
  there.
- **At least one phase** for soundness: with `Q(n) = 0`, `V_Q` accepts everything, so the
  interactive-proof statement assumes `1 ≤ Q(n)`.

## Main definitions

* `Composability.proverMoveIndex`, `Composability.verifierMoveIndex`,
  `Composability.proverMoves`: positions from message counts.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Protocol.seqProver`, `seqVerifier`, `seqRep`: the `Q`-fold sequential
  repetition.

## Main results

* `moverIsV_two_mul_add`, `countP_moverIsV`, `countP_not_moverIsV`, `exec_fst_length`,
  `exec_snd_length`, `proverMoveIndex_exec`, `verifierMoveIndex_exec`: the parties know their
  position.
* `Protocol.seqRep_exec_phase`: phase `j` of an honest execution of `π.seqRep Q` is an execution
  of `π` with the coin slices `j`.
* `ZK.seqRep`, `StatZK.seqRep` (Thm 175.1, stated; `sorry`s under the source's sketch), and
  `PerfectZK.seqRep` (proved from `StatZK.seqRep`).
* `PerfectZKAbort.seqRep`: the aborting case, derived from `PerfectZKAbort.statZK` and
  `StatZK.seqRep`, with error `Q(n) · 2^{-n}`.
* `InteractiveProof.seqRep` (stated; a `sorry` under its sketch): the repetition is an
  interactive proof.
* `InteractiveProofErr.seqRep`, `EfficientProverProofErr.seqRep` (stated; `sorry`s under their
  sketches): sequential repetition multiplies the soundness error, `s ↦ s^Q` (ruling G3-7d, for
  the text's form of Thm 124.1).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010,
  §7.2.1, Theorem 175.1 and its proof sketch (book pp. 175–176).
* [Gol01] O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography, Volume I: Basic Tools*, Cambridge University
  Press, 2001, §4.3.4 (sequential composition) and Definition 4.3.1 (perfect zero-knowledge
  with abort).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Complexity Turing

namespace Composability

/-! ### Positions -/

/-- The global index of a prover move, from the number `c` of messages it has received: with
the verifier first, the prover moves at the odd positions `2c − 1`; otherwise at `2c`. -/
def proverMoveIndex (vFirst : Bool) (c : ℕ) : ℕ := if vFirst then 2 * c - 1 else 2 * c

/-- The prover move index is `2c-1` when the verifier starts and `2c` otherwise. -/
theorem proverMoveIndex_eq (vFirst : Bool) (c : ℕ) :
    proverMoveIndex vFirst c = if vFirst then 2 * c - 1 else 2 * c := rfl

/-- The global index of a verifier move, from the number `c` of messages it has received. -/
def verifierMoveIndex (vFirst : Bool) (c : ℕ) : ℕ := if vFirst then 2 * c else 2 * c - 1

/-- The verifier move index is `2c` when the verifier starts and `2c-1` otherwise. -/
theorem verifierMoveIndex_eq (vFirst : Bool) (c : ℕ) :
    verifierMoveIndex vFirst c = if vFirst then 2 * c else 2 * c - 1 := rfl

/-- The number of prover moves among the first `k` moves. -/
def proverMoves (vFirst : Bool) (k : ℕ) : ℕ := (List.range k).countP fun t => !moverIsV vFirst t

/-- Prover moves are counted among the positions below the move budget. -/
theorem proverMoves_eq (vFirst : Bool) (k : ℕ) :
    proverMoves vFirst k = (List.range k).countP fun t => !moverIsV vFirst t := rfl

/-- The mover pattern has period `2`. -/
theorem moverIsV_two_mul_add (vFirst : Bool) (m t : ℕ) :
    moverIsV vFirst (2 * m + t) = moverIsV vFirst t := by
  cases vFirst <;> simp [moverIsV_true, moverIsV_false]

/-- The number of verifier moves among the first `g` moves. -/
theorem countP_moverIsV (vFirst : Bool) (g : ℕ) :
    (List.range g).countP (fun t => moverIsV vFirst t) =
      if vFirst then (g + 1) / 2 else g / 2 := by
  induction g with
  | zero => cases vFirst <;> simp
  | succ g ih =>
    rw [List.range_succ, List.countP_append, ih]
    cases vFirst <;> simp [moverIsV_true, moverIsV_false] <;> split_ifs <;> omega

/-- The number of prover moves among the first `g` moves. -/
theorem countP_not_moverIsV (vFirst : Bool) (g : ℕ) :
    (List.range g).countP (fun t => !moverIsV vFirst t) =
      if vFirst then g / 2 else (g + 1) / 2 := by
  induction g with
  | zero => cases vFirst <;> simp
  | succ g ih =>
    rw [List.range_succ, List.countP_append, ih]
    cases vFirst <;> simp [moverIsV_true, moverIsV_false] <;> split_ifs <;> omega

/-- After `g` moves the prover has received one message per verifier move. -/
theorem exec_fst_length (P V : Strategy) (vFirst : Bool) (x zP zV rP rV : List Bool) (g : ℕ) :
    (exec P V vFirst x zP zV rP rV g).1.length =
      (List.range g).countP (fun t => moverIsV vFirst t) := by
  induction g with
  | zero => simp
  | succ g ih =>
    rw [exec_succ, List.range_succ, List.countP_append]
    by_cases h : moverIsV vFirst g = true <;> simp [h, ih]

/-- After `g` moves the verifier has received one message per prover move. -/
theorem exec_snd_length (P V : Strategy) (vFirst : Bool) (x zP zV rP rV : List Bool) (g : ℕ) :
    (exec P V vFirst x zP zV rP rV g).2.length =
      (List.range g).countP (fun t => !moverIsV vFirst t) := by
  induction g with
  | zero => simp
  | succ g ih =>
    rw [exec_succ, List.range_succ, List.countP_append]
    by_cases h : moverIsV vFirst g = true <;> simp [h, ih]

/-- **The prover knows the global move**: when it moves at move `g`, the number of messages it
has received gives `g` back. -/
theorem proverMoveIndex_exec (P V : Strategy) (vFirst : Bool) (x zP zV rP rV : List Bool)
    (g : ℕ) (hg : moverIsV vFirst g = false) :
    proverMoveIndex vFirst (exec P V vFirst x zP zV rP rV g).1.length = g := by
  rw [exec_fst_length, countP_moverIsV]
  cases vFirst <;> simp [moverIsV_true, moverIsV_false, proverMoveIndex] at hg ⊢ <;> omega

/-- **The verifier knows the global move**: when it moves at move `g`, the number of messages
it has received gives `g` back. -/
theorem verifierMoveIndex_exec (P V : Strategy) (vFirst : Bool) (x zP zV rP rV : List Bool)
    (g : ℕ) (hg : moverIsV vFirst g = true) :
    verifierMoveIndex vFirst (exec P V vFirst x zP zV rP rV g).2.length = g := by
  rw [exec_snd_length, countP_not_moverIsV]
  cases vFirst <;> simp [moverIsV_true, moverIsV_false, verifierMoveIndex] at hg ⊢ <;> omega

end Composability

open Composability

namespace Protocol

/-! ### The sequential repetition -/

/-- The prover `P_Q`: at a real position of phase `j`, `π.P` on the coin slice `j` and the
messages received in phase `j`; at a filler position, `[]`. Its coins are `Q` copies of
`π.P`'s. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) coins next]
def seqProver (π : Protocol) (Q : PolyExpr) : Strategy where
  next x y r hist :=
    if proverMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length % (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length) <
        π.rounds.eval x.length then
      π.P.next x y
        (coinBlock (π.P.coinLen x.length)
          (proverMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length / (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length)) r)
        (hist.drop (proverMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length /
          (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length) * π.rounds.eval x.length))
    else []
  coins := .mul Q π.P.coins

/-- The verdict of `V_Q` on its complete history: `[true]` iff for every phase `j < Q`, `π.V`
on the coin slice `j` and the real messages of phase `j` outputs `[true]`. -/
def seqVerdict (π : Protocol) (Q : ℕ) (x z r : List Bool) (hist : List (List Bool)) :
    List Bool :=
  if (List.range Q).all (fun j => decide (π.V.next x z (coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length) j r)
      ((hist.drop (j * π.rounds.eval x.length)).take
        (proverMoves π.verifierFirst (π.rounds.eval x.length))) = [true]))
  then [true] else [false]

/-- The repeated verdict is true exactly when every phase's original verdict is true. -/
theorem seqVerdict_eq (π : Protocol) (Q : ℕ) (x z r : List Bool)
    (hist : List (List Bool)) :
    seqVerdict π Q x z r hist =
      if (List.range Q).all (fun j => decide
        (π.V.next x z (coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length) j r)
          ((hist.drop (j * π.rounds.eval x.length)).take
            (proverMoves π.verifierFirst (π.rounds.eval x.length))) = [true]))
      then [true] else [false] := rfl

/-- The verifier `V_Q`: on its complete history (`Q · k` messages received) its verdict
(`seqVerdict`); otherwise, at a real position of phase `j`, `π.V` on the coin slice `j` and the
messages received in phase `j`; at a filler position, `[]`. Its coins are `Q` copies of
`π.V`'s. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) coins next]
def seqVerifier (π : Protocol) (Q : PolyExpr) : Strategy where
  next x z r hist :=
    if hist.length = Q.eval x.length * π.rounds.eval x.length then
      seqVerdict π (Q.eval x.length) x z r hist
    else if verifierMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length % (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length) <
        π.rounds.eval x.length then
      π.V.next x z
        (coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length)
          (verifierMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length / (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length)) r)
        (hist.drop (verifierMoveIndex π.verifierFirst hist.length /
          (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length) * π.rounds.eval x.length))
    else []
  coins := .mul Q π.V.coins

/-- **The `Q`-fold sequential repetition** of `π` [PS10, Theorem 175.1, `(P_Q, V_Q)`]:
`Q(|x|)` phases of `2 · rounds(|x|)` moves, each running `π` on `x` with fresh coins and then
filler moves. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) P V rounds verifierFirst]
def seqRep (π : Protocol) (Q : PolyExpr) : Protocol where
  P := π.seqProver Q
  V := π.seqVerifier Q
  rounds := .mul Q (.mul (.const 2) π.rounds)
  verifierFirst := π.verifierFirst

/-- The number of moves of the repetition. -/
theorem seqRep_rounds_eval (π : Protocol) (Q : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) :
    (π.seqRep Q).rounds.eval n = 2 * π.rounds.eval n * Q.eval n := by
  simp [seqRep, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const]
  ring

/-- **Phase `j` of an honest execution of the repetition is an execution of `π`** with the coin
slices `j`: after the `j` earlier phases and the `k` real moves of phase `j`, the messages each
party received in phase `j` are those it receives in `π` with those coins.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the position `t ≤ k` in phase `j`, for the move `2kj + t`.
1. At `t = 0` each party has received exactly `jk` messages (`exec_fst_length`,
   `countP_moverIsV` with `2kj` moves), so both dropped lists are empty.
2. At a move `2kj + t` with `t < k`, the mover is `π`'s mover at `t` (`moverIsV_two_mul_add`).
   The mover recovers `2kj + t` from its message count (`proverMoveIndex_exec`,
   `verifierMoveIndex_exec`). So it computes `j` and `t < k`, and it runs `π`'s strategy on the
   slice `j` and on the messages of phase `j`, which equal `π`'s by the induction hypothesis.
   `V_Q` is not at its verdict: it has received fewer than `jk + k ≤ Qk` messages.
3. Appending the same message on both sides preserves the equation (`List.drop_append_of_le`,
   as at least `jk` messages precede it). -/
theorem seqRep_exec_phase (π : Protocol) (Q : PolyExpr) (x y z rP rV : List Bool) {j : ℕ}
    (hj : j < Q.eval x.length) :
    (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V π.verifierFirst x y z rP rV
        (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length * j + π.rounds.eval x.length)).1.drop
          (j * π.rounds.eval x.length) =
      (exec π.P π.V π.verifierFirst x y z (coinBlock (π.P.coinLen x.length) j rP)
        (coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length) j rV) (π.rounds.eval x.length)).1 ∧
    (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V π.verifierFirst x y z rP rV
        (2 * π.rounds.eval x.length * j + π.rounds.eval x.length)).2.drop
          (j * π.rounds.eval x.length) =
      (exec π.P π.V π.verifierFirst x y z (coinBlock (π.P.coinLen x.length) j rP)
        (coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length) j rV) (π.rounds.eval x.length)).2 := by
  set k := π.rounds.eval x.length with hk
  set vF := π.verifierFirst with hvF
  set sP := coinBlock (π.P.coinLen x.length) j rP
  set sV := coinBlock (π.V.coinLen x.length) j rV
  have hjk : (j + 1) * k ≤ Q.eval x.length * k := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hj
  have hjk' : (j + 1) * k = j * k + k := by ring
  have h2 : 2 * k * j = 2 * (j * k) := by ring
  suffices key : ∀ t, t ≤ k →
      (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV (2 * k * j + t)).1.drop (j * k) =
        (exec π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV t).1 ∧
      (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV (2 * k * j + t)).2.drop (j * k) =
        (exec π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV t).2 from key k le_rfl
  intro t
  induction t with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    constructor
    · rw [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le]
      · exact (congrArg Prod.fst (exec_zero π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV)).symm
      · rw [exec_fst_length, countP_moverIsV]
        cases vF <;> simp <;> omega
    · rw [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le]
      · exact (congrArg Prod.snd (exec_zero π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV)).symm
      · rw [exec_snd_length, countP_not_moverIsV]
        cases vF <;> simp <;> omega
  | succ t ih =>
    intro ht
    obtain ⟨ih₁, ih₂⟩ := ih (by omega)
    have htk : t < k := by omega
    have hl₁ : (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV (2 * k * j + t)).1.length =
        j * k + (exec π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV t).1.length := by
      rw [exec_fst_length, exec_fst_length, countP_moverIsV, countP_moverIsV]
      cases vF <;> simp <;> omega
    have hl₂ : (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV (2 * k * j + t)).2.length =
        j * k + (exec π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV t).2.length := by
      rw [exec_snd_length, exec_snd_length, countP_not_moverIsV, countP_not_moverIsV]
      cases vF <;> simp <;> omega
    have hle₂ : (exec π.P π.V vF x y z sP sV t).2.length ≤ t := by
      rw [exec_snd_length]
      exact (List.countP_le_length).trans (by simp)
    have hmv : moverIsV vF (2 * k * j + t) = moverIsV vF t := by
      rw [show 2 * k * j + t = 2 * (k * j) + t by ring]
      exact moverIsV_two_mul_add _ _ _
    have hmod : (2 * k * j + t) % (2 * k) = t := by
      rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)]
    have hdiv : (2 * k * j + t) / (2 * k) = j := by
      rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_div_left _ _ (by omega), Nat.div_eq_of_lt (by omega),
        Nat.zero_add]
    rw [show 2 * k * j + (t + 1) = (2 * k * j + t) + 1 by ring, exec_succ, exec_succ]
    simp only [hmv]
    by_cases hV : moverIsV vF t = true
    · simp only [hV, if_true]
      refine ⟨?_, ih₂⟩
      rw [List.drop_append_of_le_length (by omega), ih₁]
      congr 2
      have hidx := verifierMoveIndex_exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV
        (2 * k * j + t) (by rw [hmv]; exact hV)
      have hne : (exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV (2 * k * j + t)).2.length ≠
          Q.eval x.length * k := by omega
      show (π.seqVerifier Q).next x z rV _ = _
      simp only [seqVerifier, ← hk, ← hvF]
      rw [if_neg hne, hidx, hmod, if_pos htk, hdiv, ih₂]
    · simp only [Bool.not_eq_true] at hV
      simp only [hV, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
      refine ⟨ih₁, ?_⟩
      rw [List.drop_append_of_le_length (by omega), ih₂]
      congr 2
      have hidx := proverMoveIndex_exec (π.seqRep Q).P (π.seqRep Q).V vF x y z rP rV
        (2 * k * j + t) (by rw [hmv]; exact hV)
      show (π.seqProver Q).next x y rP _ = _
      simp only [seqProver, ← hk, ← hvF]
      rw [hidx, hmod, if_pos htk, hdiv, ih₁]

end Protocol

/-! ### Theorem 175.1 -/

variable {π : Protocol} {R : List Bool → List Bool → Prop}

/-- **Theorem 175.1, computational case** [PS10, Theorem 175.1]: the sequential repetition of a
zero-knowledge protocol with a bounded prover is zero-knowledge.

**Proof sketch** ([Gol01, §4.3.4], with the hybrids made explicit).
1. Given an efficient `V_Q*`, let `V*` be the verifier of one run of `π` whose auxiliary input
   is `⟨z, r, m̄₁, …, m̄_i⟩`: it runs `V_Q*` on the random tape `r`, feeds it the messages
   `m̄₁, …, m̄_i` of the first `i` phases (fillers `[]` included), and plays phase `i + 1` as
   `V_Q*` does. It is efficient, and it reads `i` from its auxiliary input. Let `S` be its
   simulator (`ZK π R`).
2. `S_Q(x, z)`: pick `r`; for `i = 0, …, Q − 1` run `S(x, ⟨z, r, m̄₁, …, m̄_i⟩)` and take the
   prover's messages of its output as `m̄_{i+1}`. Messages longer than `B(|x|)` are truncated;
   real ones never are (`ProverBounded`). Output `V_Q*`'s view `(x, z, r, m̄₁ … m̄_Q)`. The
   auxiliary inputs stay below `|z| + |r| + Q · k · (2B + 2)`, a polynomial `Lz'` in `|x|`, so
   `S_Q` is a strict PPT.
3. Hybrid `H_i`: the first `i` phases real, the rest simulated as in `S_Q`. `H_Q` is the real
   view, and `H_0` is `S_Q`'s output. A distinguisher between `H_i` and `H_{i+1}` gives one
   between the real and the simulated phase `i + 1`, with the first `i` real phases as auxiliary
   input (of length at most `Lz'`). It reads `i` and those phases from the sample, and completes
   phases `i + 2, …` with `S`. So it does not need the possibly inefficient prover.
4. By `ZK π R` at the bound `Lz'` the advantage is at most `Q(|x|) · ε(|x|)`, which is
   negligible. -/
theorem ZK.seqRep {B : PolyExpr} (h : ZK π R) (hB : π.ProverBounded R B) (Q : PolyExpr) :
    ZK (π.seqRep Q) R := by
  sorry

/-- **Theorem 175.1, statistical case**: statistical error `δ` composes to `Q · δ`, under the
same prover bound.

**Proof sketch.** As for `ZK.seqRep`, with statistical distance instead of a distinguisher.
Each hybrid step changes one phase from real to simulated for a fixed auxiliary input, at
distance at most `δ(|x|)` (`StatZK π R δ` holds for every auxiliary input). The common
post-processing, which completes the later phases and truncates the messages, does not increase
the distance. Summing the `Q(|x|)` steps by the triangle inequality gives `Q(|x|) · δ(|x|)`. -/
theorem StatZK.seqRep {B : PolyExpr} {δ : ℕ → ℝ} (h : StatZK π R δ)
    (hB : π.ProverBounded R B) (Q : PolyExpr) :
    StatZK (π.seqRep Q) R (fun n => Q.eval n * δ n) := by
  sorry

/-- **Theorem 175.1, perfect case**: the sequential repetition of a perfect zero-knowledge
protocol with a bounded prover is perfect zero-knowledge (`StatZK.seqRep` at `δ = 0`). -/
theorem PerfectZK.seqRep {B : PolyExpr} (h : PerfectZK π R) (hB : π.ProverBounded R B)
    (Q : PolyExpr) : PerfectZK (π.seqRep Q) R := by
  apply perfectZK_iff.mpr
  simpa only [mul_zero] using StatZK.seqRep h.statZK hB Q

/-- **Theorem 175.1, strict-PPT aborting case** [PS10, Theorem 175.1]
[Gol01, Definition 4.3.1 and §4.3.4]: the formal `PerfectZKAbort` premise gives statistical
zero-knowledge of the repetition with error `Q(n) · 2^{-n}`.

**Proof sketch.** The premise supplies a strict-PPT simulator that aborts with probability at
most `1/2` and, conditioned on success, has exactly the real view's law. First apply the proved
`PerfectZKAbort.statZK` bridge: run `n = |x|` independent retries on fresh coin blocks and keep
the first non-aborting output. The probability that all retries abort is at most `2^{-n}`;
conditioned on a retry succeeding, its output has the real view's law. This yields statistical
error `2^{-n}`. Then `StatZK.seqRep` [Gol01, §4.3.4] bounds the distance of the `Q(n)` phases by
the sum of their errors, `Q(n) · 2^{-n}`.

**Source distinction.** [PS10] uses expected-polynomial-time wording. This result instead uses
boundedly many executions of the strict-PPT aborting simulator in its formal premise; it does
not infer an exact conditional law by truncating an arbitrary expected-time simulator. -/
theorem PerfectZKAbort.seqRep {B : PolyExpr} (h : PerfectZKAbort π R)
    (hB : π.ProverBounded R B) (Q : PolyExpr) :
    StatZK (π.seqRep Q) R (fun n => Q.eval n * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n) := by
  simpa only [one_div] using StatZK.seqRep h.statZK hB Q

/-- **The repetition of an interactive proof is an interactive proof** [PS10, Theorem 175.1,
"`(P_Q, V_Q)` is an interactive proof"], when every input length has at least one phase.

**Proof sketch.**
1. *Efficiency:* `V_Q` runs `π.V`'s machine on a coin slice and a suffix of its history, or
   `Q(|x|)` times for its verdict, so it is computed by a uniform machine with coins `Q · coins`.
2. *Completeness:* with the witness `y` of `π`, each phase is an honest execution of `π` with
   independent uniform coin slices (`seqRep_exec_phase`), accepted with probability one, so
   every phase accepts.
3. *Soundness:* for `x ∉ L` and a prover `P'`, phase `0` is an execution of `P'` against `π.V`
   on the coin slice `0`, which is uniform. Here the dropped prefix is empty, so
   `seqRep_exec_phase`'s argument applies with `P'` in place of `π.P`. Phase `0`'s verdict is
   `[false]` with probability `> 1 − ε(|x|)`, and then `V_Q` outputs `[false]`. Phase `0`
   exists since `1 ≤ Q(|x|)`. -/
theorem InteractiveProof.seqRep {L : Language Bool} (h : InteractiveProof π L) (Q : PolyExpr)
    (hQ : ∀ n, 1 ≤ Q.eval n) : InteractiveProof (π.seqRep Q) L := by
  sorry

/-- **Sequential repetition multiplies the soundness error** [PS10, p. 120: the protocol "can be
repeated many times … to drive the probability of error as low as desired"; and p. 127, the
`O(n|E|)` repetitions of the 3-colouring protocol]: if `π` has soundness error `s`, its
`Q`-phase sequential repetition (which accepts iff every phase does) has soundness error
`s(|x|)^{Q(|x|)}`, with perfect completeness kept.

**Proof sketch.**
1. *Efficiency and completeness* as in `InteractiveProof.seqRep`: every phase of the honest
   execution is an honest execution of `π` with independent coin slices
   (`seqRep_exec_phase`), accepted with probability one.
2. *Soundness:* fix `x ∉ L`, a prover `P'` and `z`. Condition on the prover's coins and on the
   transcript of phases `0, …, j − 1`. Phase `j` is then an execution, against `π.V` on a fresh
   uniform coin slice, of the prover strategy that `P'` induces with that prefix hard-wired (the
   verifier reads only phase `j`'s messages). By `π`'s soundness it accepts with probability at
   most `s(|x|)`, whatever the prefix. By induction on `j`, all `Q(|x|)` phases accept with
   probability at most `s(|x|)^{Q(|x|)}`, so `V_Q` outputs `[false]` with probability at least
   `1 − s(|x|)^{Q(|x|)}`. -/
theorem InteractiveProofErr.seqRep {L : Language Bool} {s : ℕ → ℝ} (h : InteractiveProofErr π L s)
    (Q : PolyExpr) (hQ : ∀ n, 1 ≤ Q.eval n) :
    InteractiveProofErr (π.seqRep Q) L (fun n => s n ^ Q.eval n) := by
  sorry

/-- **The efficient-prover form**: the sequential repetition of an interactive proof with an
efficient prover and soundness error `s` is one with soundness error `s^Q`; the repeated prover
is efficient and complete for every witness.

**Proof sketch.** `InteractiveProofErr.seqRep` for the proof system; `P_Q` runs `π.P`'s machine
on its coin slice and a suffix of its history, so a uniform machine computes it; completeness for
every witness phase by phase, as in `InteractiveProof.seqRep`. -/
theorem EfficientProverProofErr.seqRep {L : Language Bool} {s : ℕ → ℝ}
    (h : EfficientProverProofErr π L R s) (Q : PolyExpr) (hQ : ∀ n, 1 ≤ Q.eval n) :
    EfficientProverProofErr (π.seqRep Q) L R (fun n => s n ^ Q.eval n) := by
  sorry

end TCSlib.Cryptography

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Composability/SimNonMalleable.lean =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability.NonMalleable
import Mathlib.Tactic.Simps.Basic

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Simulation-based non-malleability (statement phase)

[PS10, Definition 173.7 and Theorem 174.8], in the form of [PSV07] (ruling of 2026-11-05: the
non-malleability notions of §7.1.5–7.1.6 follow Pass, shelat and Vaikuntanathan).

**Why not the source's form.** As written, Theorem 174.8 is false (inventory Thm-174.8).
- Definition 173.7's simulator `S(1^n, z)` gets no public key. An adversary that outputs a fresh
  `Enc_pk(0^n)` hits the relation `R(m) = {0^n}` with probability 1, while a simulator without
  `pk` produces a ciphertext that decrypts to `0^n` under a fresh key only with the probability
  of guessing one.
- The quantifiers of Definitions 172.6 and 173.7 do not line up: adaptive `m₀, m₁` in one, a
  fixed `m` in the other.

**The form taken: SIM-NME′ at one message** [PSV07, Definition 1, with `ℓ = 1`; "single-message
security" there].
- *Real.* `(pk, sk) ← Gen(1^n)`; `(M, s) ← A₁^{O₁}(pk)`; `m ← M`; `y ← Enc_pk(m)`;
  `((c₁, …, c_r), σ) ← A₂^{O₂}(y, h(m), s)`; output `(M, m, (d₁, …, d_r), σ)` with
  `d_i = COPY` if `c_i = y` and `d_i = Dec_sk(c_i)` otherwise (possibly `⊥`: invalid ciphertexts
  are allowed, the "′" of [PSV07]).
- *Ideal.* `(pk, sk) ← Gen(1^n)`; `(M, s) ← S₁(pk)`; `m ← M`; `((c₁, …, c_r), σ) ← S₂(h(m), s)`;
  output `(M, m, (d₁, …, d_r), σ)` with `d_i = COPY` if `c_i = COPY` and `Dec_sk(c_i)` otherwise.
- *Security.* For every history function `h`, every adversary `A` and all polynomials `r`, there
  is a simulator `S` whose experiment no distinguisher tells from `A`'s. [PSV07] replaces the
  relations `R` of [PS10] and [DDN00] by distinguishers ("any p.p.t. distinguisher can be
  described as a p.p.t. relation and vice versa", remarks after Definition 2).

**The encoding.**
- *Phases and oracles* are those of Definition 171.5: the challenge query separates `A₁` from
  `A₂`, and `Dec` answers per the attack (`decOpen`), refusing the challenge.
- *The sampler.* [PSV07]'s `A₁` outputs a machine `M`. Here a sampler `M` (a machine with a
  history function, `MsgSampler`) is quantified together with `A`, and `A₁` outputs a parameter
  `a`, with `m = M(a)` read at `msgLen(n)` bits. The output carries `a` in place of `M`'s
  description. With `M` a universal clocked machine this is [PSV07]'s form, and the fixed
  lengths make every sampler valid in [PSV07]'s sense.
- *The simulator* is one oracle machine on `pk`. Its single query `a` is answered by `h(m)`,
  where `m = M(a)` is drawn by the experiment: `S₁` is its run up to the query, `S₂` the rest. It
  has no `Dec` oracle under any attack, as in [PSV07]. Each of its `r` outputs is a `COPY` flag
  and a ciphertext.
- *No challenge.* If the machine never queries, its parameter is `0^{pl(n)}` and `m = M(0^{pl(n)})`
  (in both experiments).

**Theorem 174.8.** [PSV07] proves that SIM-NME′ and IND-NME′ (Definition 172.6 at many messages)
coincide **under CPA** (its Theorem 3), and that SIM-NME′ is **strictly stronger under CCA1 and
CCA2**, even at one message (its Theorem 4). It always implies IND-NME′ (its Corollary 1). So
Theorem 174.8 is stated under CPA, with the implication SIM ⇒ IND for every attack. [PSV07]
defers both proofs to its full version; the sketches below are the maintainer's.

## Main definitions

* `MsgSampler`: a message sampler with a history function.
* `FixedLengthPKScheme.snmReal`, `FixedLengthPKScheme.snmIdeal`: the two experiments.
* `FixedLengthPKScheme.SimNMSecure`: [PS10, Definition 173.7] as [PSV07, Definition 1].

## Main results

* `FixedLengthPKScheme.nmSecure_of_simNMSecure` (stated; a `sorry` under its sketch):
  SIM ⇒ IND for every attack [PSV07, Corollary 1].
* `FixedLengthPKScheme.simNMSecure_of_nmSecure_cpa` (stated; a `sorry` under its sketch):
  IND ⇒ SIM under CPA [PSV07, Theorem 3].
* `FixedLengthPKScheme.simNMSecure_cpa_iff_nmSecure_cpa`: Theorem 174.8 under CPA, from the two.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010,
  §7.1.6, Definition 173.7 and Theorem 174.8 (book pp. 173–174).
* [PSV07] R. Pass, a. shelat, V. Vaikuntanathan, *Relations among notions of non-malleability for
  encryption*, ASIACRYPT 2007, LNCS 4833, pp. 519–535: Definitions 1–4, Theorems 3 and 4,
  Corollary 1.
* [PSV06] R. Pass, a. shelat, V. Vaikuntanathan, *Construction of a non-malleable encryption
  scheme from any semantically secure one*, CRYPTO 2006, LNCS 4117, pp. 271–289: Definition 3.
* [DDN00] D. Dolev, C. Dwork, M. Naor, *Nonmalleable cryptography*, SIAM J. Comput. 30(2), 2000
  (cited through [PSV07]).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability

open Complexity Turing TCSlib.Cryptography TCSlib.Cryptography.Games

/-- **A message sampler with a history function** [PSV07, Definition 1]: a machine `M` activated
on a `paramLen(n)`-bit parameter, whose output is the message, and a polynomial-time history
function `h`, read at `histLen(n)` bits. -/
structure MsgSampler where
  /-- The sampler, activated on the adversary's parameter. -/
  samp : NUPPT
  /-- The length of the parameter. -/
  paramLen : PolyExpr
  /-- The history function `h`. -/
  hist : List Bool → List Bool
  /-- The length at which `h(m)` is read. -/
  histLen : PolyExpr
  /-- `h` is polynomial-time. -/
  hist_poly : PolyTimeComputable hist

namespace MsgSampler

variable (M : MsgSampler)

/-- The message `m = M(a)` with the sampler's coins `ρ`, read at `ℓ` bits. -/
def draw (ℓ n : ℕ) (a : Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool) (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) : Fin ℓ → Bool :=
  padFin ℓ (M.samp.runAt n (List.ofFn a) ρ)

/-- Drawing a message pads the sampler's output on parameter `a` and coins `ρ` to `ℓ` bits. -/
theorem draw_eq (ℓ n : ℕ) (a : Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool) (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) :
    M.draw ℓ n a ρ = padFin ℓ (M.samp.runAt n (List.ofFn a) ρ) := rfl

/-- The history `h(m)`, read at `histLen(n)` bits. -/
def histAt {ℓ : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (m : Fin ℓ → Bool) : Fin (M.histLen.eval n) → Bool :=
  padFin _ (M.hist (List.ofFn m))

/-- The sampled message's history is `M.hist (List.ofFn m)`, padded to `histLen(n)` bits. -/
theorem histAt_eq {ℓ : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (m : Fin ℓ → Bool) :
    M.histAt n m = padFin (M.histLen.eval n) (M.hist (List.ofFn m)) := rfl

/-- The simulator's oracle at parameter `n`: the parameter in, the history out. -/
abbrev simSpec (n : ℕ) : OracleSpec (Fin 1) :=
  bitSpec (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)

/-- The simulator's oracle is `bitSpec` with parameter-length queries and history-length
answers. -/
theorem simSpec_eq (n : ℕ) :
    M.simSpec n = bitSpec (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n) := rfl

end MsgSampler

namespace FixedLengthPKScheme

variable (S : FixedLengthPKScheme)

/-! ### The real experiment -/

/-- The query lengths of the real experiment's oracles `Dec` and `Challenge`. -/
def snmInLens (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) : Fin 2 → ℕ
  | 0 => S.ctLen.eval n
  | 1 => M.paramLen.eval n

/-- A real-experiment decryption query has `ctLen(n)` bits. -/
theorem snmInLens_zero (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmInLens M n 0 = S.ctLen.eval n := rfl

/-- A real-experiment challenge query has `paramLen(n)` bits. -/
theorem snmInLens_one (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmInLens M n 1 = M.paramLen.eval n := rfl

/-- The answer lengths: `Dec` answers a validity flag and a message; `Challenge` the challenge
ciphertext and the history. -/
def snmOutLens (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) : Fin 2 → ℕ
  | 0 => S.msgLen.eval n + 1
  | 1 => S.ctLen.eval n + M.histLen.eval n

/-- A real-experiment decryption answer has one validity bit followed by `msgLen(n)` bits. -/
theorem snmOutLens_zero (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmOutLens M n 0 = S.msgLen.eval n + 1 := rfl

/-- A real-experiment challenge answer has `ctLen(n) + histLen(n)` bits. -/
theorem snmOutLens_one (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmOutLens M n 1 = S.ctLen.eval n + M.histLen.eval n := rfl

/-- The two oracles of the real experiment at parameter `n`. -/
abbrev snmSpec (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) : OracleSpec (Fin 2) :=
  bitSpec (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n)

/-- The real experiment's oracle specification is `bitSpec` at its published query and
answer lengths. -/
theorem snmSpec_eq (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmSpec M n = bitSpec (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) := rfl

/-- The state of the real experiment's oracles: the challenge, with the parameter it was asked
on, once asked. -/
abbrev SnmState (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  Option ((Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) × (Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool))

/-- The real oracle state is an optional pair of a `ctLen(n)`-bit ciphertext and a
`paramLen(n)`-bit sampler parameter. -/
theorem SnmState_eq (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) :
    S.SnmState M n =
      Option ((Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) × (Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool)) := rfl

/-- **The oracles of the real experiment** at parameter `n`, for the keys `pk`, `sk` and the
sampler's coins `ρ`.
- `Dec` answers as in Definition 171.5: `⟨1, Dec_sk(c)⟩` when it is open (`decOpen`) and `c` is
  not the challenge, and `⊥` (all `false`) otherwise.
- `Challenge` on the parameter `a`, the first time: `m = M(a; ρ)`, `y ← Enc_pk(m)`; it answers
  `⟨y, h(m)⟩` and records `(y, a)`. Later it repeats the recorded answer. -/
noncomputable def snmImpl (atk : Attack) (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (pk sk : List Bool)
    (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) : QueryImpl (S.snmSpec M n) (S.SnmState M n) unifSpec
  | 0, c, s =>
    if FixedLengthScheme.decOpen atk s.isSome && !decide (s.map Prod.fst = some c) then
      .pure (FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer (decodeFin _ (S.dec (pairEncode sk (List.ofFn c)))), s)
    else .pure (zeroBits _, s)
  | 1, a, s =>
    match s with
    | some (y, a₀) => .pure (Fin.append y (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a₀ ρ)), s)
    | none =>
      (ProbComp.sample (S.enc.Coins n)).bind fun re =>
        let y : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool :=
          padFin _ (S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode pk (List.ofFn (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ))) re)
        .pure (Fin.append y (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)), some (y, a))

/-- A real-experiment decryption query returns the encoded decryption exactly when the oracle
is open and the ciphertext is not the recorded challenge; otherwise it returns all-false bits. -/
theorem snmImpl_dec (atk : Attack) (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (pk sk : List Bool)
    (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) (c : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) (s : S.SnmState M n) :
    S.snmImpl atk M n pk sk ρ 0 c s =
      if FixedLengthScheme.decOpen atk s.isSome && !decide (s.map Prod.fst = some c) then
        .pure (FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer
          (decodeFin (S.msgLen.eval n) (S.dec (pairEncode sk (List.ofFn c)))), s)
      else .pure (zeroBits (S.msgLen.eval n + 1), s) := rfl

/-- A real-experiment challenge query repeats the recorded ciphertext and history when a
challenge exists; otherwise it encrypts the sampled message and records the ciphertext and
parameter [PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem snmImpl_challenge (atk : Attack) (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (pk sk : List Bool)
    (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) (a : Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool) (s : S.SnmState M n) :
    S.snmImpl atk M n pk sk ρ 1 a s =
      match s with
      | some (y, a₀) => .pure (Fin.append y (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a₀ ρ)), s)
      | none =>
        (ProbComp.sample (S.enc.Coins n)).bind fun re =>
          let y : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool :=
            padFin (S.ctLen.eval n)
              (S.enc.runAt n (pairEncode pk (List.ofFn (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ))) re)
          .pure (Fin.append y (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)), some (y, a)) := rfl

/-- Under CPA, `Dec` never answers. -/
theorem snmImpl_dec_cpa (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (pk sk : List Bool) (ρ : M.samp.Coins n)
    (c : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) (s : S.SnmState M n) :
    S.snmImpl .cpa M n pk sk ρ 0 c s = .pure (zeroBits _, s) := by
  simp [snmImpl, FixedLengthScheme.decOpen_cpa]

/-- The codec of the adversary: the two oracles, and a final output of `r` ciphertexts followed by
an `sl`-bit `σ`. -/
def snmCodec (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) :
    MachineCodec (S.snmSpec M n) (Fin (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) → Bool) :=
  bitCodec (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl)

/-- The real-experiment codec uses `decodeBitMove` with `r * ctLen(n) + sl` output bits. -/
theorem snmCodec_decodeMove (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    (S.snmCodec M n r sl).decodeMove w =
      decodeBitMove (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) w :=
  bitCodec_decodeMove (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) w

/-- The real-experiment codec encodes a log entry `(i, x, y)` as `⟨1^i, ⟨x, y⟩⟩`. -/
theorem snmCodec_encodeEntry (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ)
    (e : Σ i, (S.snmSpec M n).dom i × (S.snmSpec M n).rng i) :
    (S.snmCodec M n r sl).encodeEntry e =
      pairEncode (List.replicate e.1 true) (pairEncode (List.ofFn e.2.1) (List.ofFn e.2.2)) :=
  bitCodec_encodeEntry (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) e

/-- When its query budget expires, the real-experiment codec returns
`zeroBits (r * ctLen(n) + sl)`. -/
theorem snmCodec_timeout (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) :
    (S.snmCodec M n r sl).timeout = zeroBits (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) :=
  bitCodec_timeout (S.snmInLens M n) (S.snmOutLens M n) (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl)

/-- The `i`-th of the `r` ciphertexts in an adversary's output. -/
def snmCt {n r sl : ℕ} (w : Fin (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) → Bool) (i : Fin r) :
    Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool :=
  fun j => w (Fin.castAdd sl (finProdFinEquiv (i, j)))

/-- Real output ciphertext `i` has bit `j` at `Fin.castAdd sl (finProdFinEquiv (i, j))`. -/
theorem snmCt_eq {n r sl : ℕ} (w : Fin (r * S.ctLen.eval n + sl) → Bool) (i : Fin r) :
    S.snmCt w i = fun j => w (Fin.castAdd sl (finProdFinEquiv (i, j))) := rfl

/-- The final `σ`: the last `sl` bits of an output. -/
def snmSigma {k sl : ℕ} (w : Fin (k + sl) → Bool) : Fin sl → Bool :=
  fun j => w (Fin.natAdd k j)

/-- The final output string's bit `j` is input bit `Fin.natAdd k j`. -/
theorem snmSigma_eq {k sl : ℕ} (w : Fin (k + sl) → Bool) :
    snmSigma w = fun j => w (Fin.natAdd k j) := rfl

/-- **The entry `d_i`** [PSV07, Definition 1]: `COPY` if `copy`, and `Dec_sk(c)` otherwise.
Encoded as a `COPY` flag followed by `Dec`'s answer (a validity flag and the message; all `false`
for `⊥`). -/
def snmEntry {n : ℕ} (sk : List Bool) (copy : Bool) (c : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) :
    Fin (S.msgLen.eval n + 1 + 1) → Bool :=
  if copy then Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Bool) true (zeroBits _)
  else Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Bool) false
    (FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer (decodeFin _ (S.dec (pairEncode sk (List.ofFn c)))))

/-- An entry begins with its COPY flag; a copy has an all-false payload, and every other entry
has the encoded decryption as payload [PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem snmEntry_eq {n : ℕ} (sk : List Bool) (copy : Bool) (c : Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) :
    S.snmEntry sk copy c =
      if copy then Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Bool) true (zeroBits (S.msgLen.eval n + 1))
      else Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Bool) false
        (FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer
          (decodeFin (S.msgLen.eval n) (S.dec (pairEncode sk (List.ofFn c))))) := rfl

/-- **The output `(M, m, (d₁, …, d_r), σ)`** handed to the distinguisher, with the parameter `a`
in place of `M`: the concatenation of its fixed-length parts. -/
def snmView {n pl r sl : ℕ} (a : Fin pl → Bool) (m : Fin (S.msgLen.eval n) → Bool)
    (d : Fin r → Fin (S.msgLen.eval n + 1 + 1) → Bool) (σ : Fin sl → Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn a ++ List.ofFn m ++ (List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn (d i)).flatten ++ List.ofFn σ

/-- The distinguisher's view concatenates the parameter, sampled message, flattened entries,
and final `σ` [PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem snmView_eq {n pl r sl : ℕ} (a : Fin pl → Bool) (m : Fin (S.msgLen.eval n) → Bool)
    (d : Fin r → Fin (S.msgLen.eval n + 1 + 1) → Bool) (σ : Fin sl → Bool) :
    S.snmView a m d σ =
      List.ofFn a ++ List.ofFn m ++ (List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn (d i)).flatten ++ List.ofFn σ :=
  rfl

/-- **The real experiment** `SIM-NME′(Π, A, n)` [PSV07, Definition 1, `ℓ = 1`] for the attack
`atk`, the sampler `M`, query budget `q`, `r` output ciphertexts and an `sl`-bit `σ`, followed
by the distinguisher `D`: sample the keys and the coins, run `A` on `pk` against the oracles, and
output `D`'s verdict on `(a, m, (d_i)_i, σ)`, where `d_i` is `COPY` on a copy of the challenge. -/
noncomputable def snmReal (atk : Attack) (M : MsgSampler) (A : NUPPT) (q r sl : ℕ) (D : NUPPT)
    (n : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool :=
  (ProbComp.sample (S.gen.Coins n)).bind fun rg =>
  (ProbComp.sample (M.samp.Coins n)).bind fun ρ =>
  (ProbComp.sample (A.Coins n)).bind fun rA =>
  (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins n)).bind fun rD =>
  (simulate
      (S.snmImpl atk M n (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) ρ)
      (A.toCompOn (S.snmCodec M n r sl) n q (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) rA) none).bind
    fun res =>
      let a := (res.2.map Prod.snd).getD (zeroBits _)
      .pure (D.distinguisherL n
        (S.snmView a (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)
          (fun i => S.snmEntry (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg))
            (decide (res.2.map Prod.fst = some (S.snmCt res.1 i))) (S.snmCt res.1 i))
          (snmSigma res.1)) rD)

/-- The real simulation experiment samples all coins, runs the adversary against its oracles,
and applies the distinguisher to the resulting parameter, message, entries, and final output
[PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem snmReal_eq (atk : Attack) (M : MsgSampler) (A : NUPPT) (q r sl : ℕ) (D : NUPPT)
    (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmReal atk M A q r sl D n =
      (ProbComp.sample (S.gen.Coins n)).bind (fun rg =>
      (ProbComp.sample (M.samp.Coins n)).bind fun ρ =>
      (ProbComp.sample (A.Coins n)).bind fun rA =>
      (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins n)).bind fun rD =>
      (simulate
          (S.snmImpl atk M n (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) ρ)
          (A.toCompOn (S.snmCodec M n r sl) n q (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) rA) none).bind
        fun res =>
          let a := (res.2.map Prod.snd).getD (zeroBits (M.paramLen.eval n))
          .pure (D.distinguisherL n
            (S.snmView a (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)
              (fun i => S.snmEntry (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg))
                (decide (res.2.map Prod.fst = some (S.snmCt res.1 i))) (S.snmCt res.1 i))
              (snmSigma res.1)) rD)) := rfl

/-! ### The ideal experiment -/

/-- **The oracle of the ideal experiment**: on the parameter `a` (the first one asked, recorded),
the history `h(m)` of `m = M(a; ρ)`. -/
noncomputable def simImpl (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) :
    QueryImpl (M.simSpec n) (Option (Fin (M.paramLen.eval n) → Bool)) unifSpec :=
  fun _ a s => .pure (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n (s.getD a) ρ), some (s.getD a))

/-- The ideal oracle returns the history of the sampled message at the recorded parameter,
or at the current query if no parameter has been recorded, and records that parameter. -/
theorem simImpl_eq (M : MsgSampler) (n : ℕ) (ρ : M.samp.Coins n) :
    S.simImpl M n ρ =
      fun _ a s => .pure
        (M.histAt n (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n (s.getD a) ρ), some (s.getD a)) := rfl

/-- The codec of the simulator: its one oracle, and a final output of `r` entries, each a `COPY`
flag and a ciphertext, followed by an `sl`-bit `σ`. -/
def simCodec (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) :
    MachineCodec (M.simSpec n) (Fin (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) → Bool) :=
  bitCodec (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)
    (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl)

/-- The ideal-experiment codec uses `decodeBitMove` with parameter and history lengths and
`r * (ctLen(n) + 1) + sl` output bits. -/
theorem simCodec_decodeMove (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    (S.simCodec M n r sl).decodeMove w =
      decodeBitMove (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)
        (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) w :=
  bitCodec_decodeMove (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)
    (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) w

/-- The ideal-experiment codec encodes a log entry `(i, x, y)` as `⟨1^i, ⟨x, y⟩⟩`. -/
theorem simCodec_encodeEntry (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ)
    (e : Σ i, (M.simSpec n).dom i × (M.simSpec n).rng i) :
    (S.simCodec M n r sl).encodeEntry e =
      pairEncode (List.replicate e.1 true) (pairEncode (List.ofFn e.2.1) (List.ofFn e.2.2)) :=
  bitCodec_encodeEntry (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)
    (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) e

/-- When its query budget expires, the ideal-experiment codec returns
`zeroBits (r * (ctLen(n) + 1) + sl)`. -/
theorem simCodec_timeout (M : MsgSampler) (n r sl : ℕ) :
    (S.simCodec M n r sl).timeout = zeroBits (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) :=
  bitCodec_timeout (fun _ => M.paramLen.eval n) (fun _ => M.histLen.eval n)
    (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl)

/-- The `i`-th entry of the simulator's output: its `COPY` flag and its ciphertext. -/
def simEntry {n r sl : ℕ} (w : Fin (r * (S.ctLen.eval n + 1) + sl) → Bool) (i : Fin r) :
    Bool × (Fin (S.ctLen.eval n) → Bool) :=
  (w (Fin.castAdd sl (finProdFinEquiv (i, 0))),
    fun j => w (Fin.castAdd sl (finProdFinEquiv (i, j.succ))))

attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false }) fst snd] simEntry

/-- **The ideal experiment** `SIM-NME′‾(Π, S, n)` [PSV07, Definition 1, `ℓ = 1`] for the sampler
`M`, `r` output entries and an `sl`-bit `σ`, followed by the distinguisher `D`: sample the keys
and the coins, run the simulator on `pk` against the history oracle with one query, and output
`D`'s verdict on `(a, m, (d_i)_i, σ)`, where `d_i` is `COPY` on a flagged entry and `Dec_sk(c_i)`
otherwise. -/
noncomputable def snmIdeal (M : MsgSampler) (Sim : NUPPT) (r sl : ℕ) (D : NUPPT) (n : ℕ) :
    ProbComp Bool :=
  (ProbComp.sample (S.gen.Coins n)).bind fun rg =>
  (ProbComp.sample (M.samp.Coins n)).bind fun ρ =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Sim.Coins n)).bind fun rS =>
  (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins n)).bind fun rD =>
  (simulate (S.simImpl M n ρ)
      (Sim.toCompOn (S.simCodec M n r sl) n 1 (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) rS) none).bind
    fun res =>
      let a := res.2.getD (zeroBits _)
      .pure (D.distinguisherL n
        (S.snmView a (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)
          (fun i => S.snmEntry (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) (S.simEntry res.1 i).1
            (S.simEntry res.1 i).2)
          (snmSigma res.1)) rD)

/-- The ideal simulation experiment samples all coins, runs the simulator against the history
oracle, and applies the distinguisher to the parameter, message, decoded entries, and final
output [PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem snmIdeal_eq (M : MsgSampler) (Sim : NUPPT) (r sl : ℕ) (D : NUPPT) (n : ℕ) :
    S.snmIdeal M Sim r sl D n =
      (ProbComp.sample (S.gen.Coins n)).bind (fun rg =>
      (ProbComp.sample (M.samp.Coins n)).bind fun ρ =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Sim.Coins n)).bind fun rS =>
      (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins n)).bind fun rD =>
      (simulate (S.simImpl M n ρ)
          (Sim.toCompOn (S.simCodec M n r sl) n 1 (pairFstD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) rS) none).bind
        fun res =>
          let a := res.2.getD (zeroBits (M.paramLen.eval n))
          .pure (D.distinguisherL n
            (S.snmView a (M.draw (S.msgLen.eval n) n a ρ)
              (fun i => S.snmEntry (pairSndD (S.gen.runAt n [] rg)) (S.simEntry res.1 i).1
                (S.simEntry res.1 i).2)
              (snmSigma res.1)) rD)) := rfl

/-! ### Definition 173.7 and Theorem 174.8 -/

/-- **Simulation-based non-malleability** [PS10, Definition 173.7], in the form SIM-NME′ of
[PSV07, Definition 1] at one message, under the attack `atk`: for every sampler `M` (with its
history function), every non-uniform PPT adversary `A`, every polynomial query budget `q`,
number `r` of output ciphertexts and length `sl` of `σ`, there is a non-uniform PPT simulator
whose ideal experiment every non-uniform PPT distinguisher tells from `A`'s real one with
negligible advantage. -/
def SimNMSecure (atk : Attack) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : MsgSampler) (A : NUPPT) (q r sl : PolyExpr), ∃ Sim : NUPPT,
    ∀ D : NUPPT, ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧ ∀ n,
      advantage (S.snmReal atk M A (q.eval n) (r.eval n) (sl.eval n) D n)
        (S.snmIdeal M Sim (r.eval n) (sl.eval n) D n) ≤ ε n

/-- Simulation-based non-malleability holds exactly when, for every sampler, adversary and
polynomial budgets, one simulator makes every distinguisher's real/ideal advantage negligible
[PS10, Definition 173.7; PSV07, Definition 1]. -/
theorem SimNMSecure_iff (atk : Attack) :
    S.SimNMSecure atk ↔
      ∀ (M : MsgSampler) (A : NUPPT) (q r sl : PolyExpr), ∃ Sim : NUPPT,
        ∀ D : NUPPT, ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ, Negligible ε ∧ ∀ n,
          advantage (S.snmReal atk M A (q.eval n) (r.eval n) (sl.eval n) D n)
            (S.snmIdeal M Sim (r.eval n) (sl.eval n) D n) ≤ ε n := Iff.rfl

/-- **Theorem 174.8, (relation-based ⇒ indistinguishability-based), for every attack**
[PSV07, Corollary 1, at one message]: SIM-NME′ implies Definition 172.6.

**Proof sketch** (the maintainer's; [PSV07] defers its proof).
1. Fix an NM adversary `A` (budget `q`, `ℓ` ciphertexts) and a distinguisher `D`. Take the
   sampler `M` with parameter `⟨m₀, m₁⟩` that outputs `m_β` for a uniform coin `β`, and the
   constant history. The adversary `A'` runs `A`, forwarding `Dec`; on `A`'s challenge
   `⟨m₀, m₁⟩` it asks its own challenge with that parameter and passes `y` on. It outputs `A`'s
   ciphertexts, with `sl = 0`.
2. In the real experiment `m = m_β`, `y ← Enc_pk(m_β)`, and the entries `d_i` are `NM_β`'s
   output once `COPY` is read as `⊥`. Let `D'` read `m₀, m₁, m` from the view, output `0` when
   `m₀ = m₁`, and otherwise output whether `D`'s verdict on the converted entries equals `β`.
   Then `Pr[D' = 1] = ½ + ½ (Pr[D(NM_1) = 1] − Pr[D(NM_0) = 1])` on the event `m₀ ≠ m₁`
   (when `m₀ = m₁`, `NM_0` and `NM_1` coincide).
3. In the ideal experiment the simulator's entries depend on `pk`, its coins and the constant
   history, so they are independent of `β` given the parameter; `D'` accepts with probability
   `½` on the event `m₀ ≠ m₁`. The distinguisher `D''` that tests `m₀ ≠ m₁` bounds the
   difference of that event's probabilities. So `NM`'s advantage is at most twice the sum of
   `D'`'s and `D''`'s, both negligible. -/
theorem nmSecure_of_simNMSecure (atk : Attack) (h : S.SimNMSecure atk) : S.NMSecure atk := by
  sorry

/-- **Theorem 174.8, (indistinguishability-based ⇒ relation-based), under CPA** [PSV07,
Theorem 3, at one message]: Definition 172.6 implies SIM-NME′ under a chosen-plaintext attack.
(Under CCA1 and CCA2 it does not, [PSV07, Theorem 4].)

**Proof sketch** (the maintainer's; [PSV07] defers its proof). Fix `M`, `A`, `q`, `r`, `sl`.
1. **The simulator** runs `A` on `pk`, answering `Dec` with `⊥` (CPA, `snmImpl_dec_cpa`). On
   `A`'s challenge `a` it asks its own query `a`, gets `h(m)`, draws a dummy `m̃ ← M(a)` with its
   own coins (it can run `M`), and answers `A` with `⟨Enc_pk(m̃), h(m)⟩`. It outputs `A`'s
   ciphertexts, flagging those equal to its dummy challenge, and `σ`. If `A` never asks, it
   never queries and outputs `A`'s output unflagged. At `msgLen(n) = 0` the two experiments
   coincide.
2. **The two experiments differ only in the challenge**: `Enc_pk(m)` in the real one,
   `Enc_pk(m̃)` in the ideal one, with `m, m̃` independent draws from `M(a)`, and the same `h(m)`.
3. **The NM adversary** `B` runs `A`; at `a` it draws `m, m̃ ← M(a)`, asks its challenge on
   `⟨m, m̃⟩`, receives `y = Enc_pk(m_b)`, and answers `A` with `⟨y, h(m)⟩`. It outputs `A`'s
   ciphertexts, then for each bit `x` of `a`, `m`, `σ` and the copy flags `[c_i = y]`, the pair
   `Enc_pk(x^{msgLen})`, `Enc_pk((¬x)^{msgLen})`. The two plaintexts differ, so by correctness at
   most one of the pair is the challenge, and the NM view yields `x` (as in the sketch of
   Theorem 175.9).
4. From `NM_b`'s view, the distinguisher reconstructs `(a, m, (d_i)_i, σ)`: the real experiment's
   output for `b = 0`, and the ideal one's (with the simulator of step 1) for `b = 1`. So `D`'s
   advantage is `B`'s NM advantage, negligible. -/
theorem simNMSecure_of_nmSecure_cpa (h : S.NMSecure .cpa) : S.SimNMSecure .cpa := by
  sorry

/-- **Theorem 174.8 under CPA** [PS10, Theorem 174.8; PSV07, Theorem 3, at one message]:
non-malleability (Definition 172.6) and simulation-based non-malleability (Definition 173.7, as
SIM-NME′) coincide under a chosen-plaintext attack. -/
theorem simNMSecure_cpa_iff_nmSecure_cpa : S.SimNMSecure .cpa ↔ S.NMSecure .cpa :=
  ⟨S.nmSecure_of_simNMSecure .cpa, S.simNMSecure_of_nmSecure_cpa⟩

end FixedLengthPKScheme

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability.SequentialZK
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.ThreeColoring.Simulator

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Negligible soundness error for sequential 3-colouring

The quadratic repetition estimate for the sequential 3-colouring construction of
[PS10, Proposition 127.6 and Theorem 175.1].

## Contents

* The eventual dyadic bound for the repeated soundness error.

## Main definitions

The repetition count is `PolyExpr.normal 2 2`, which evaluates to `2 * (N + 1)^2`.

## Main results

* `Composability.negligible_colSeqSound`: raising `1 - 1/N + 2^{-N}` to this repetition
  count gives a negligible function of `N`.
* `Composability.colSeq_efficientProverProof_zk`: the resulting efficient-prover proof and
  computational zero-knowledge corollary.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (Proposition 127.6 and Theorem 175.1.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §1.2 (negligible functions).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability

open Complexity

/-- The function `(1 - 1/N + (1/2)^N)^{2(N+1)^2}` is negligible: the quantitative estimate
for sequential repetition of the formal 3-colouring soundness bound
[PS10, Proposition 127.6 and Theorem 175.1], with the repetition count fixed explicitly.

**Proof sketch.** The dyadic function is negligible, so twice it is eventually smaller than
`1/N`. Beyond that threshold and `N = 0`, the one-run bound is nonnegative and at most
`1 - 1/(2N)`. This latter base lies in `[0, 1]`, and `2(N+1)^2 ≥ N(2N)`, so the repeated
bound is at most `(1 - 1/(2N))^{N(2N)} ≤ exp(-N) ≤ 2^{-N}`. Eventual domination by the
dyadic negligible function proves the claim; no estimate at `N = 0` is needed. -/
theorem negligible_colSeqSound :
    Negligible (fun N => (1 - 1 / (N : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N) ^
      ((PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval N)) := by
  have hdyad : Negligible (fun N : ℕ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N) := by
    simpa only [one_div] using negligible_two_pow_neg
  obtain ⟨N₀, htail⟩ := ((negligible_iff _).mp (hdyad.const_mul 2)) 1
  refine hdyad.mono ⟨max N₀ 1, ?_⟩
  intro N hN
  have hN₀ : N₀ ≤ N := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hN
  have hN₁ : 1 ≤ N := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hN
  have hN₁R : (1 : ℝ) ≤ N := by exact_mod_cast hN₁
  have hd : 0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N := by positivity
  -- The degree-one tail of twice the dyadic error absorbs half the inverse gap.
  have hscaled : 2 * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N < 1 / (N : ℝ) := by
    have hmul : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N := by positivity
    simpa only [pow_one, abs_of_nonneg hmul] using htail N hN₀
  have hrec : 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ) = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (1 / (N : ℝ)) := by
    rw [Nat.cast_mul, ← one_div_mul_one_div]
    norm_num
  have hsmall : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N ≤ 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    rw [hrec]
    linarith only [hscaled]
  have hinv : 1 / (N : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by
    simpa only [div_one] using one_div_le_one_div_of_le zero_lt_one hN₁R
  have ha : 0 ≤ 1 - 1 / (N : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N := by
    linarith only [hinv, hd]
  have hab : 1 - 1 / (N : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N ≤
      1 - 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    rw [hrec] at hsmall ⊢
    linarith only [hsmall]
  have hb₀ : 0 ≤ 1 - 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ) := ha.trans hab
  have hb₁ : 1 - 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 1 :=
    sub_le_self _ (by positivity)
  -- A larger exponent decreases a power whose base lies in the unit interval.
  have hexponent : N * (2 * N) ≤ (PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval N := by
    rw [PolyExpr.eval_normal]
    nlinarith
  calc
    |(1 - 1 / (N : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N) ^ ((PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval N)| =
        (1 - 1 / (N : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N) ^ ((PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval N) :=
      abs_of_nonneg (pow_nonneg ha _)
    _ ≤ (1 - 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ ((PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval N) :=
      pow_le_pow_left₀ ha hab _
    _ ≤ (1 - 1 / ((2 * N : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ (N * (2 * N)) :=
      pow_le_pow_of_le_one hb₀ hb₁ hexponent
    _ ≤ Real.exp (-(N : ℝ)) :=
      one_sub_inv_pow_mul_le_exp (2 * N) N (by omega)
    _ ≤ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ N := exp_neg_le_inv_two_pow N
    _ = |(1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ N| := by
      rw [abs_of_nonneg hd, one_div]

/-- Quadratic sequential repetition of the commitment-based 3-colouring protocol is an
interactive proof with an efficient prover and is computational zero-knowledge
[PS10, Theorem 124.1, Propositions 127.6 and 128.8, Theorem 175.1].

**Deviation.** The phase count is the explicit polynomial `2(N+1)^2` in the encoded input
length, rather than the graph-dependent `n|E|` of the source. This is a larger sufficient
repetition count for the formal one-run bound `1 - 1/N + 2^{-N}`. The sequential protocol
uses the filler scheduling of `Protocol.seqRep`, not `colProtocolRep`.

**Proof sketch.** Apply sequential repetition to the efficient-prover proof with its
explicit one-run soundness error. The preceding estimate makes the repeated error negligible,
so the error-parametric proof gives an interactive proof. The original proof's bounded honest
prover messages supply the hypothesis of zero-knowledge composition, which applies to
`col_zk`. The generic repetition statements remain the campaign's admitted fill targets. -/
theorem colSeq_efficientProverProof_zk {Com : List Bool → List Bool} {ℓ : PolyExpr}
    (hC : Commitment Com ℓ) :
    EfficientProverProof ((colProtocol Com ℓ).seqRep (.normal 2 2)) L3COL R3COL ∧
      ZK ((colProtocol Com ℓ).seqRep (.normal 2 2)) R3COL := by
  have hQ : ∀ n, 1 ≤ (PolyExpr.normal 2 2).eval n := by
    intro n
    rw [PolyExpr.eval_normal]
    exact Nat.succ_le_of_lt (by positivity)
  have hbase := col_efficientProverProofErr hC
  have hrep := EfficientProverProofErr.seqRep hbase (.normal 2 2) hQ
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := hbase.boundedP
  exact ⟨EfficientProverProofErr.efficientProverProof negligible_colSeqSound hrep,
    ZK.seqRep (col_zk hC) hB (.normal 2 2)⟩

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Probability
import TCSlib.InformationTheory.StatisticalDistance

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Concrete security experiments

The concrete layer fixes one value of the security parameter and quantifies over all
adversaries, given as functions of their input and of a uniformly random coin string
from a finite type `ρ`. No running time is imposed here; efficiency is the job of the
asymptotic layer. The experiments are:

* inversion: on `f x` for uniform `x`, output some preimage of `f x`;
* prediction: on `f x`, output the bit `B x`;
* distinguishing: tell apart samples `X s` and `Y t` from uniform seeds `s` and `t`.

Samplers `X : σ → γ` from a finite seed type `σ` describe exactly the distributions
that are pushforwards of uniform coins, which covers every efficiently samplable
ensemble at a fixed parameter.

## Main definitions

* `invProb f A`: the probability that `A` inverts `f`.
* `predProb f B A`: the probability that `A` predicts `B` from `f`.
* `acceptProb X D`: the probability that `D` accepts a sample of `X`.
* `distAdv X Y D`: the distinguishing advantage of `D` between `X` and `Y`.

## Main results

* `acceptProb_comp_equiv`: relabelling the seeds by a bijection preserves acceptance.
* `abs_sum_sub_le_statDist`: a test set distinguishes two distributions by at most
  their statistical distance.
* `distAdv_le_statDist`: the distinguishing advantage of any distinguisher is at most
  the statistical distance of the sampled distributions.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, Definition 2.1 (inversion), Definition 2.3 (prediction),
  Definitions 3.2–3.4 and Lemma 3.1 (distinguishing).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset TCSlib.InformationTheory

variable {α β ρ σ τ γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ]

/-- The probability that the adversary `A`, given `f x` for uniform `x` and uniform coins
`r`, outputs a preimage of `f x`. [Gar26, Definition 2.1, Equation (2.1)], at one value of
the security parameter; the input `1^n` is implicit in the fixed types. -/
noncomputable def invProb (f : α → β) (A : β → ρ → α) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun z : α × ρ => f (A (f z.1) z.2) = f z.1

/-- The probability that the adversary `A`, given `f x` for uniform `x` and uniform coins
`r`, outputs the bit `B x`. [Gar26, Definition 2.3], at one value of the security
parameter. -/
noncomputable def predProb (f : α → β) (B : α → Bool) (A : β → ρ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun z : α × ρ => A (f z.1) z.2 = B z.1

/-- The probability that the distinguisher `D` with uniform coins accepts a sample `X s`
for a uniform seed `s`. [Gar26, Definitions 3.2 and 3.4], the quantities `p(n)` and
`q(n)`. -/
noncomputable def acceptProb (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun z : σ × ρ => D (X z.1) z.2 = true

/-- The distinguishing advantage of `D` between the sampled distributions `X` and `Y`,
`|Pr[D(X) = 1] - Pr[D(Y) = 1]|`. [Gar26, Definitions 3.2 and 3.4], the quantity
`Δ_A(n)`. -/
noncomputable def distAdv (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  |acceptProb X D - acceptProb Y D|

/-! ### Defining equations

Published so that other layers (the `Games` bridges) read the experiments through stated
equations rather than through their bodies. -/

/-- The defining equation of `invProb`: `invProb f A = Pr_{(x, r)}[f(A(f x, r)) = f x]`, over
uniform `(x, r) ∈ α × ρ`. -/
theorem invProb_def (f : α → β) (A : β → ρ → α) :
    invProb f A = uprob fun z : α × ρ => f (A (f z.1) z.2) = f z.1 := rfl

/-- The defining equation of `predProb`: `predProb f B A = Pr_{(x, r)}[A(f x, r) = B x]`, over
uniform `(x, r) ∈ α × ρ`. -/
theorem predProb_def (f : α → β) (B : α → Bool) (A : β → ρ → Bool) :
    predProb f B A = uprob fun z : α × ρ => A (f z.1) z.2 = B z.1 := rfl

/-- The defining equation of `acceptProb`: `acceptProb X D = Pr_{(s, r)}[D(X s, r) = 1]`, over
uniform `(s, r) ∈ σ × ρ`. -/
theorem acceptProb_def (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X D = uprob fun z : σ × ρ => D (X z.1) z.2 = true := rfl

/-- The defining equation of `distAdv`: `distAdv X Y D = |acceptProb X D - acceptProb Y D|`. -/
theorem distAdv_def (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y D = |acceptProb X D - acceptProb Y D| := rfl

/-- Relabelling the seed space of a sampler by a bijection does not change the probability
that a distinguisher accepts: a bijective image of a uniform seed is uniform. -/
theorem acceptProb_comp_equiv (e : σ ≃ τ) (X : τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun s => X (e s)) D = acceptProb X D :=
  uprob_comp_equiv (e.prodCongr (Equiv.refl ρ)) (fun z : τ × ρ => D (X z.1) z.2 = true)

/-- The probability that a uniform seed `s` has `X s` in an event `q` is the mass of `q` under
the pushforward of the uniform distribution along `X`. Technical glue between `uprob` and
`FinDist.map`.

**Proof sketch.** Both sides equal `∑ s, [q (X s)] / |σ|`: on the right, group the seeds
by their image under `X`. -/
theorem uprob_comp_eq_sum_map [Nonempty σ] [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] (X : σ → γ)
    (q : γ → Prop) [DecidablePred q] :
    uprob (fun s => q (X s)) = ∑ g ∈ univ.filter q, (FinDist.uniform σ).map X g := by
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, sum_filter]
  have h := Finset.sum_fiberwise' univ X
    (fun g => if q g then (Fintype.card σ : ℝ)⁻¹ else 0)
  have h2 : ∑ s, (if q (X s) then (Fintype.card σ : ℝ)⁻¹ else 0) =
      ((univ.filter fun s => q (X s)).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card σ := by
    rw [← sum_filter, sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, div_eq_mul_inv]
  rw [← h2, ← h]
  refine sum_congr rfl fun g _ => ?_
  split_ifs <;> simp [FinDist.map_apply]

/-- The acceptance probability of `D` on samples of `X` is the average over the coins `r` of
the mass, under the distribution of `X`, of the set of samples that `D` accepts with coins
`r`. Technical glue for `distAdv_le_statDist`.

**Proof sketch.** Swap the two coordinates of the sample space, apply Fubini
(`uprob_prod`) to average over the coins first, and rewrite each section with
`uprob_comp_eq_sum_map`. -/
theorem acceptProb_eq_uexp_sum_map [Nonempty σ] [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] (X : σ → γ)
    (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X D = uexp (fun r : ρ => ∑ g ∈ univ.filter (fun g => D g r = true),
        (FinDist.uniform σ).map X g) := by
  rw [acceptProb, ← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm ρ σ), uprob_prod]
  congr 1
  funext r
  exact uprob_comp_eq_sum_map X (fun g => D g r = true)

/-- For any set `T` of outcomes, `|p(T) - q(T)|` is at most the statistical distance of `p`
and `q`. This is the deterministic case of [Gar26, Lemma 3.1].

**Proof sketch.** The differences `d = p - q` sum to zero, so the sum of `d` over the
complement of `T` is `-d(T)`. Splitting `∑ |d|` over `T` and its complement and applying
the triangle inequality to each part gives `∑ |d| ≥ 2 |d(T)|`. -/
theorem abs_sum_sub_le_statDist [Fintype γ] (p q : FinDist γ) (T : Finset γ) :
    |∑ g ∈ T, (p g - q g)| ≤ statDist p q := by
  classical
  have h0 : ∑ g, (p g - q g) = 0 := by
    rw [sum_sub_distrib, p.sum_prob, q.sum_prob, sub_self]
  have hsplit := sum_add_sum_compl T (fun g => p g - q g)
  have habs := sum_add_sum_compl T (fun g => |p g - q g|)
  have h1 := abs_sum_le_sum_abs (fun g => p g - q g) T
  have h2 := abs_sum_le_sum_abs (fun g => p g - q g) Tᶜ
  have hneg : ∑ g ∈ Tᶜ, (p g - q g) = -∑ g ∈ T, (p g - q g) := by linarith
  rw [hneg, abs_neg] at h2
  rw [statDist_eq]
  linarith

/-- The distinguishing advantage of any distinguisher, deterministic or with coins, is at
most the statistical distance of the two sampled distributions. [Gar26, Lemma 3.1].

**Proof sketch.** Average over the coins (`acceptProb_eq_uexp_sum_map`): for fixed coins
`r` the distinguisher is a test set `T_r`, whose advantage is `|X(T_r) - Y(T_r)|`. By
`abs_sum_sub_le_statDist` each of these is at most the statistical distance, and the
absolute value of an average is at most the average of the absolute values. -/
theorem distAdv_le_statDist [Nonempty σ] [Nonempty τ] [Nonempty ρ] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq γ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y D ≤
      statDist ((FinDist.uniform σ).map X) ((FinDist.uniform τ).map Y) := by
  have hρ : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card ρ := Nat.cast_pos.2 Fintype.card_pos
  rw [distAdv, acceptProb_eq_uexp_sum_map X, acceptProb_eq_uexp_sum_map Y, uexp_def, uexp_def,
    ← sub_div, ← sum_sub_distrib, abs_div, abs_of_pos hρ, div_le_iff₀ hρ]
  refine (abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans ?_
  rw [mul_comm, ← nsmul_eq_mul, ← card_univ, ← sum_const]
  refine sum_le_sum fun r _ => ?_
  rw [← sum_sub_distrib]
  exact abs_sum_sub_le_statDist _ _ _

end TCSlib.Cryptography
